items.title: Otti urges Abia residents to reject election-season promises by politicians
items.description: Gov. Alex Otti of Abia has urged voters to resist financial and material inducements from politicians, warning that such offers could undermine the state’s future in the 2027 general elections. Otti gave the warning on Sunday at the 2nd Session of the 7th Synod of the Anglican Communion, Diocese of Aba Ngwa North, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi-Umuocham, Aba. The governor, represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Caleb Ajagba, charged citizens to prioritise long-term development over immediate material benefits offered by politicians. He alleged that politicians responsible for the state’s challenges over 24 years were returning to seek voters’ support. Otti warned against allowing such politicians to derail the progress his administration was pursuing. “The people that created a problem that God now had to answer your prayer by sending someone after His own heart, are all over again. “But the Bible says surely they shall proceed no further. Please, let us be careful.When God opens a door, may we not close it. “Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years, because even prayer and fasting will not open it. “May we not lose what God has given to us on the platter,” he said. The governor also urged Christians to remain vigilant, warning that some politicians who previously neglected the Church were seeking its attention. “Like we have been told the season is here again and politicians are everywhere and as the Bible says we are not ignorant of the devices of the enemy. “These are devices, because many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church. “Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said. Otti said the first three years of his administration had focused largely on laying a foundation for development, adding that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would prioritise consolidation. “Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins. “What will now be happening is consolidation and beauty will emerge. “This present house (Abia State) you are seeing today, in the next four years, you will know that God has really come to tabernacle in the midst of man. “Today Abia State has become a point of reference,” he said. On the church’s development projects, Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support towards their completion. He, however, reiterated that public funds should be deployed to develop the state rather than finance religious projects. The governor commended the guest speaker for delivering what he described as an appropriate and unadulterated message, urging Christians to verify information and examine issues critically before reaching conclusions. He said the synod’s theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts Chapter 17 verse 11 to 12, was relevant as the country approached another political season. “As Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation; especially our state,” he said. Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Anglican Communion, Dr Nathan Kanu, said the theme challenged Christians to move beyond hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely. Kanu commended Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities, presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings on his administration. In his sermon, the Guest Speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Rt. Rev. Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to think critically before taking action. Speaking on: “The Bereans Wisdom,” with his text from Acts chapter 17 verse 12 and 15, Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was timely and encouraged believers to examine messages rather than accept or reject them without reflection. “The theme of the synod is very important and apt in this our time, it didn’t say throw it away, it says think through it,” he said. Oparajiaku regretted that Christians, who were expected to demonstrate sound judgement, sometimes fell victim to deception. “When members of the church know the Bible they would not be deceived. “This is because the church refused to behave like the Bereans. The Bereans Christian never took everything for granted they always thought through whatever they heard,” he said. The Bishop thanked God for giving Abia the opportunity to be governed by Otti, whom he credited with changing the state’s narrative. The synod attracted dignitaries, including the Labour Party’s National Vice-Chairman, South-East, Hon. Ishmael Onuoha; state chairman, Sir Peter Azubuike; and Osisioma Local Government Area Mayor, Hon. Chidi Agu. Others were the Special Assistant to the Governor on Special Duties, Dr George Chiedozie; Special Adviser to the Governor on Labour Matters, Godson Anucha; and Aba industrialist, Mr Bob Udeagha. items.title: GPL 2026/27: Medeama go three clear as Hearts of Oak recover and Bechem stage stunning comeback
items.description: Medeama strengthened their position at the top of the Premier League with a commanding 3-1 victory over Heart of Lions, while Hearts of Oak returned to winning ways and Bechem United produced an impressive comeback on an eventful Matchday Six. Emmanuel Annor opened the scoring before Kingsley Braye struck twice in the 64th and 65th minutes to secure Medeama’s victory against Heart of Lions at the TnA Stadium. Kofi Mawutodzi Agbadji grabbed a consolation for Heart of Lions, but the champions moved to 14 points, three clear of second-placed Hearts of Oak. The Phobians climbed to second after Frank Duku’s header earned them a hard-fought 1-0 win over newly promoted Port City, ending their two-game winless run. The result ended Samartex’s unbeaten start and extended AshantiGold’s impressive home league run to 18 matches without defeat. items.title: Concours de recrutement de 6 000 enseignants en Guinée : les épreuves avancées au 17 octobre 2026
items.description: Le gouvernement guinéen a annoncé l’avancement de la date des épreuves du concours de recrutement direct de 6 000 nouveaux enseignants, initialement prévues le mercredi 21 octobre 2026. Selon un communiqué du ministère de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique, signé au nom du ministre porte-parole du gouvernement, les candidats composeront finalement le samedi 17 octobre 2026, sur instruction du président de la République, chef de l’État. Cette décision intervient dans un contexte marqué par le démarrage effectif de l’année scolaire 2026-2027 et traduit, selon les autorités, la volonté d’accélérer le processus de recrutement afin de répondre rapidement aux besoins en personnel enseignant dans les établissements scolaires du pays. Organisé pour le compte du ministère de l’Éducation nationale, de l’Alphabétisation, de l’Enseignement technique et de la Formation professionnelle, ce concours vise à renforcer les effectifs des enseignants et à améliorer la disponibilité du personnel éducatif, notamment dans les établissements situés à l’intérieur du pays. Le communiqué précise que les épreuves se dérouleront exclusivement à l’intérieur du territoire national, dans les chefs-lieux des préfectures de Kindia, Boké, Mamou, Labé, Kankan, N’Zérékoré et Faranah. Chaque candidat devra se présenter dans le centre qui lui sera attribué. La liste définitive des candidats retenus indiquera les centres de composition correspondants et sera publiée ultérieurement. Les autorités rappellent également que les enseignants recrutés à l’issue de cette sélection seront affectés exclusivement dans les établissements scolaires situés à l’intérieur du pays. Une orientation qui vise à répondre aux besoins en personnel enseignant dans les localités concernées et à soutenir le fonctionnement du système éducatif sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Autre point important pour les candidats : la période d’inscription reste ouverte jusqu’au dimanche 11 octobre 2026 à 23 h 59, conformément au communiqué initial. Les personnes souhaitant participer au concours sont donc invitées à finaliser leurs démarches dans le délai imparti et à vérifier attentivement les informations relatives à leur candidature. Le ministère souligne par ailleurs que toutes les autres dispositions du communiqué initial demeurent inchangées. Les informations concernant les centres d’examen et les modalités pratiques de déroulement des épreuves seront communiquées aux candidats par les canaux officiels.

items.title: Ntiamoah Foundation launches “BEYOND 20” anniversary campaign
items.description: Ntiamoah Foundation has launched BEYOND 20: From Impact to Legacy, a year-long campaign marking two decades of improving lives through education, health, and community development, while setting out its vision for the future. Established in 2006 by the Entrepreneur, Robert Kwaku Appiah Asante (R.K.A. Asante), Ntiamoah Foundation has worked primarily with communities in the Birim North and Birim South Districts of the Eastern Region. Its interventions span early childhood literacy, Reading Clubs and libraries, ICT education, scholarships, menstrual and maternal health, support for health facilities, and community outreach. Over the past two decades, the Ntiamoah Foundation has invested over GH¢23 million in today’s value in improving access to education, healthcare and community support. This investment has supported 34 schools and nearly 6,500 young readers, strengthened 14 Community-based health planning and services (CHPS) facilities, supported 436 life-changing surgeries and reached over 8,000 girls through menstrual health programmes, to name a few. Together, these achievements reflect a 20-year commitment to creating opportunities and improving lives in underserved communities. Launching the anniversary campaign, Executive Director Mercy Quansah-Ansah said the milestone provides an opportunity to reflect on the Foundation’s impact and set the direction for its next chapter. “Twenty years gives us much to celebrate, but BEYOND 20 is also about asking what we can put in place today that will still be changing lives twenty years from now. For us, that is the shift from impact to legacy: creating opportunities today that can continue to transform lives for generations to come.” As part of the campaign launch, the Foundation has unveiled a 20th-anniversary identity and redesigned website, which will serve as a platform for impact stories, programme updates, anniversary activities and opportunities for individuals and organisations to support its work. Building the Next Chapter Throughout the anniversary year, Ntiamoah Foundation will continue its established education and health programmes while introducing three flagship initiatives designed to turn twenty years of impact into a legacy. Programme B.E.A.M. will become the Foundation’s flagship education model, bringing together literacy, life skills, creativity, digital learning, leadership and community support to develop confident, ethical and future-ready young people. It builds on two decades of investment in Reading Clubs, libraries, ICT and other educational interventions. The Foundation will also launch the R.K.A. Asante Scholarship Scheme, a permanent programme established in honour of its founder. Beyond financial support, the scheme will combine scholarships with mentorship, leadership and professional development and community service. To commemorate the 20th anniversary, 20 for 20 Awards will select the first twenty scholars, creating the inaugural cohort of what the Foundation hopes will become a lifelong community of future leaders committed to giving back. The third flagship initiative is the Legacy Project, a long-term investment in community spaces and infrastructure that will continue serving people beyond the anniversary year. The project will create spaces to preserve local history and heritage, advance learning and leadership, and build skills and opportunities for young people. It will also include recreational infrastructure, beginning with 3 multipurpose community centres to promote youth development, healthy lifestyles and community connection. Board Chair Dr. Kojo Pumpuni Asante said the next chapter will require an even broader community of partners: “Ntiamoah’s journey has always been built on partnership. As we look beyond twenty, we invite individuals, institutions and organisations who share our belief in the power of education and health to join us. The next chapter is about multiplying opportunity and building something that future generations can inherit and build upon.” Derek Boateng, Senior Manager for Sustainability and External Relations for Zijin Golden Ridge Limited, one of the Foundation’s longstanding partners, congratulated Ntiamoah Foundation on the milestone: “Over the years, we have witnessed Ntiamoah Foundation’s commitment to improving educational outcomes, strengthening healthcare delivery and creating opportunities for vulnerable communities. Its impact can be seen not only in the projects delivered, but in the lives transformed. We congratulate the Foundation on twenty years of service and look forward to continuing our partnership.” A Year of Celebration and Legacy BEYOND 20 will spotlight the people, partnerships and communities that have shaped Ntiamoah Foundation’s journey, while mobilising support for its next chapter. The anniversary year will culminate in a Fundraising Gala Dinner and Thanksgiving Service in December, bringing together partners, donors, community leaders, beneficiaries and other stakeholders to celebrate twenty years of service and support the Foundation’s future programmes. BEYOND 20 is both a celebration of what has been achieved and an invitation to help build what comes next .

items.title: Peter Obi faults Tinubu’s 30-day petrol discount, calls policy reactive
items.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ((NDC), Peter Obi, has criticised the 30-day petrol discount announced by the President Bola Tinubu-led federal government, describing the initiative as a reactive policy that fails to address the economic hardship facing Nigerians. Obi, in a post on X, said the temporary discount was an attempt to substitute “political optics for sound policy”, arguing that the government had failed to properly assess the effects of its economic reforms. He said he delayed commenting on the announcement to allow time to assess its outcomes before concluding that the policy reflected what he described as a confused approach to governance. Obi recalled that Tinubu removed the petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, without adequate consultation or assessment of its potential impact on the economy and the livelihoods of ordinary Nigerians. He also faulted the subsequent floating of the naira and tax reforms, saying the policies were poorly sequenced and implemented. According to him, the combined effects of the policies included rising inflation, higher prices of goods and services, increasing poverty, unemployment and insecurity, as well as widening inequality and the migration of young Nigerians. “Collectively, these policies stoked inflation in all sectors, pushing in most cases unbearable price hikes across board which placed severe shocks and other adverse consequences on Nigerians,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor accused the federal government of failing to conduct and publish detailed regulatory impact assessments of its policies. He argued that such assessments would enable the government to consult stakeholders and citizens and develop more inclusive and sustainable economic strategies. Obi also questioned the potential impact of the petrol discount, which he described as less than five per cent of fuel costs. “What really does the President Bola Tinubu-led government want to achieve with a one-month discount of less than 5% on fuel cost. Will it reduce poverty, unemployment, insecurity, and inequality? Will it increase productivity and exports?” he asked. He further questioned whether the initiative was intended to test public reaction to a possible restoration of subsidy or was politically motivated ahead of the 2027 elections. Obi concluded his criticism by saying the government had raised too many questions about the policy without providing answers. Dans son nouveau livre « Décolonisations, 1925-2026 : des chemins vers l'indépendance aux conflits de mémoire », coécrit avec Sandrine Lemaire et Nicolas Bancel, l'historien Pascal Blanchard retrace un siècle de bouleversements politiques, de luttes et de violences. items.title: Credit Risk Management Directive: BoG to begin implementation for banks, others from July 1, 2027
items.description: The Bank of Ghana from 1 st July 2027 will begin the implementation of the Credit Risk Management Directive for all Banks, Savings and Loans, Finance Houses and Financial Holding Firms. The broad objective of the directive is to enhance the resilience of Regulated Financial Institutions (RFIs) by ensuring that they establish and fully implement adequate and effective credit risk management systems that commensurate with their risk-taking activities and capital strength. The specific objectives are to ensure that RFIs develop an appropriate framework for the management of their credit risk by establishing an appropriate credit risk environment, among others. According to the Central Bank, the RFIs shall align their credit risk management practices with the requirements of this Directive. However, in assessing the quality of RFIs’ their risk management of credit risk, the BOG will take into account the principle of proportionality. In particular, the assessment will be aimed at ensuring that RFIs’ credit risk management processes and tools are commensurate with profile, systemic importance, market and macroeconomic conditions as well as the scale and complexity of their activities, among others. Governance and Risk Management Framework The Bank of Ghana said the Board of RFIs shall bear the ultimate responsibility for the credit risk assumed by the RFI and for ensuring the existence and ongoing effectiveness of the credit risk management framework. Similarly, the Board shall review and approve the RFI’s credit risk appetite, credit risk management strategy, as well as credit policies, procedures, controls and management information system (MIS) at least annually or whenever there are material changes, to ensure continued adequacy, relevance and effectiveness. Roles and Responsibilities of the Senior Management The Central Bank said the Senior Management of an RFI shall be responsible for implementing the Board-approved credit risk management strategy and for establishing, maintaining, and enforcing appropriate policies and processes for identifying, measuring, monitoring, reporting, and controlling or mitigating credit risk. Such policies and processes shall cover all credit related activities of the RFI and apply at both the individual exposure and portfolio levels. The Senior Management’s responsibility for implementing the credit risk management strategy and operationalising the RFI’s credit risk policies includes ensuring that credit origination, credit assessment, approval, monitoring, and review responsibilities are clearly defined, properly assigned, and supported by appropriate segregation of duties. According to the Bank of Ghana, the effective management of credit risk within a comprehensive risk management framework is fundamental to the safety and soundness of banks, finance houses, savings and loans companies or financial holding companies regulated under the Bank and Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions Act, 2016 (Act 930), hereinafter referred to as RFIs. Over the past two decades, global financial developments have underscored the critical importance of robust credit risk management frameworks in safeguarding the stability of the financial system. Events such as the 2008-2009 global financial crisis revealed how weak credit underwriting standards, excessive leverage, and inadequate risk governance can rapidly translate into widespread loan defaults and systemic distress. The Ghanaian banking sector clean-up exercise in 2017-2019 also highlighted significant deterioration in asset quality and, consequently, pressure on capital and liquidity resulting from weaknesses in underwriting standards, risk management, governance, and related-party practices. Conversely, RFIs that established and adhered to sound credit risk management practices demonstrated stronger financial resilience.

items.title: Mbah, Nnaji, Ohaa, 13 others make INEC list for Enugu governorship
items.description: Gov. Peter Mbah, former Minister, Chief Uchenna Nnaji, and former Federal Permanent Secretary, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa, are among 16 candidates listed for the 2027 Enugu governorship election. The candidates, representing various political parties, are seeking to control the state’s Government House. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) displayed the final list at its Enugu headquarters on Sunday. The document contains the personal credentials of all 16 candidates contesting the state’s top political office. Mbah, the incumbent governor contesting on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), will face Nnaji of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). Other contenders include Ohaa of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Chief Obodoeze Ocho of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The list also names Mr Edwin Alor of Accord, Prof. Jehu Nnaji of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), and Mr Okwudilichukwu Ugwu of the Labour Party (LP). Other candidates are Mr Nnamdi Ugwu of the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), Mr Anthony Udeani of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), and Mr Afamefuna Ani of the Action Peoples Party (APP). Mr Elvis Ugwoke of the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP), Mr Friday Iloka of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), and Mr Nnamdi Omeje of the Action Democratic Party (ADP) are also contesting. The remaining candidates are Mr Ken Ikeh of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Chief Obioma Nnamani of the Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party, and Mr Ndubuisi Okonkwo of the National Rescue Movement (NRM). The candidates have intensified statewide electioneering activities, engaging stakeholders and elder statesmen ahead of the 2027 governorship election. Mbah is expected to campaign on his administration’s projects, programmes and social interventions as he seeks re-election. Government sources described the administration’s “verifiable projects and social interventions impacting the people” as key strengths ahead of the poll. The election is shaping up to be a crowded contest, with Mbah facing 15 challengers seeking to wrest control of Enugu State from the APC. The post Mbah, Nnaji, Ohaa, 13 others make INEC list for Enugu governorship appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack
items.description: A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, a day after an attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations there. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. The Iran-backed group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”. Hours later, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire. Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added. AFP journalists and locals reported hearing the sound of multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday. “The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city. The civil aviation authority said the attack caused an unspecified number of injuries, and that a damage assessment was under way. It later reported another attack on Dammam airport in the east — which the Houthis also said they had targeted — a day after the Saudi coalition reported a projectile landing nearby. – ‘Full-fledged war crime’ – The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport — where three people were also killed on Thursday — as well as on Saudi oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. Although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through. “Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University. The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”. Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday. Saturday’s attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the “horrific terrorist attack”. Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 people wounded. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before. – Operations suspended – Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source said, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 2100 GMT. A second aviation source confirmed the halt in operations “until further notice”, adding radar and communications equipment was damaged and runways needed to be assessed. Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath. “People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP. “Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood.” The attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said. The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport, while Australia urged its citizens on Sunday to stay indoors altogether and “shelter in place”. – Fighting in Yemen – Saturday’s airport strike, on the eve of Saudi Arabia’s high-profile convention and entertainment season, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing. With the summer heat subsiding, October also usually marks the beginning of the high travel season for Umrah pilgrims, with millions of Muslims from across the world flocking to Mecca. Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa. Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”. On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said Saturday. The Houthis claimed to have repelled them. Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult. bur/smw/rh The post Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lola : la police démantèle un réseau présumé de trafic de chanvre indien, trois personnes interpellées
items.description: La police a saisi 223 kilogrammes de chanvre indien et de graines de la même plante à Lola, lors d'une opération menée vendredi matin dans le quartier Woroya-Po. Trois personnes ont été interpellées dans le cadre de la lutte contre le trafic de stupéfiants. L'intervention, conduite vers 6 h par la Brigade spéciale d'intervention de la police (BSIP-Lola) sur instruction du commissaire central, le colonel Ibrahima Kéoulen Traoré, a permis de saisir 123 kg de chanvre indien et 100 kg de graines. Les agents ont aussi récupéré un fusil de calibre 12, une voiture Peugeot, une moto TVS et divers autres objets. Les trois présumés mis en cause, Blèla Goumou cultivateur à Woroya-Po, Moriba Loua et Tonhon Gouhara, domiciliée à Tinghen-Mo 1, ont été présentés à la presse ce week-end, au commissariat central, en présence de la BSIP, de la gendarmerie et de l'armée. L'un d'eux, Moriba Loua, a reconnu les faits « Je suis chaudronnier, actuellement il n'y a pas de travail, donc je travaille avec mes amis dans cette affaire de chanvre indien. » a-t-il rappelé. « Notre service a été informé de l'existence d'un réseau de trafiquants à Lola, plus précisément dans le quartier Woroya-Po », a expliqué le colonel Traoré, qui a appelé la population à collaborer. « Sans [elle], notre mission sera difficile à atteindre » a-t-il souligné. Il faut rappeler que cette opération s'inscrit dans le renforcement de la lutte contre l'insécurité à Lola. Depuis l'arrivée des nouveaux responsables du commissariat central, la lutte contre les activités illicites et la protection des populations font partie des priorités affichées.

items.title: Ghana Brands Awards 2026: Leading brands, business trailblazers to shine on November 20
items.description: Ghana’s leading brands, outstanding businesses, visionary entrepreneurs and industry trailblazers will take centre stage on November 20, 2026, as the Ghana Brands Awards (GBA) prepares to celebrate excellence, innovation and outstanding business performance across the country. Powered by the Chartered Institute of Project Analysts and Consultants (CIPAC), GBA is a prestigious awards programme dedicated to recognising businesses and individuals whose achievements are making a meaningful contribution to Ghana’s economic growth, industry development and national progress. The awards will provide a platform to celebrate organisations that are setting new standards in their respective industries through strong leadership, operational excellence, quality service delivery, innovation and a commitment to sustainable growth. Beyond celebrating established brands, GBA seeks to spotlight the entrepreneurs, business leaders and industry professionals whose vision, investment and achievements are creating opportunities, strengthening competitiveness and shaping the future of Ghana’s business environment. A Platform to Celebrate Excellence and Build Brands The Ghana Brands Awards aims to become a leading platform for recognising business excellence and promoting a culture of achievement across Ghana’s private and public sectors. The initiative seeks to honour businesses that have played a defining role in advancing their industries, setting benchmarks in sustainability, operational performance, customer service and innovation. It will also recognise outstanding projects and individual achievements that distinguish businesses from their competitors and deliver measurable value to customers, investors, employees and the wider economy. By bringing together leading players from different sectors, GBA will offer an opportunity to celebrate the local and international companies contributing to Ghana’s economic transformation while encouraging healthy competition, stronger corporate standards and continuous improvement. For participating organisations, the awards represent an opportunity to showcase their achievements, strengthen brand visibility and position themselves among the businesses setting the pace for excellence in Ghana. 24 Awards Categories to Celebrate Industry Trailblazers The 2026 edition will recognise outstanding performance across a broad range of industries, reflecting the diversity and growing potential of Ghana’s economy. The proposed awards categories include: Banking, Finance and Insurance Bank of the Year Community Bank of the Year Microfinance Bank of the Year Development Bank of the Year Debt Collection Company of the Year Insurance Company of the Year – General Insurance Company of the Year – Life Health Insurance Company of the Year Corporate Pension Trust of the Year Securities and Investment Company of the Year Industry, Energy and Infrastructure Manufacturing Company of the Year Petroleum Company of the Year – Upstream Petroleum Company of the Year – Downstream Real Estate Company of the Year Postal and Courier Services Company of the Year Shipping Company of the Year Mining Company of the Year Healthcare, Pharmaceuticals and Consumer Products Diagnostics Company of the Year Pharmaceutical Company of the Year Herbal Medicine Manufacturing Company of the Year Beverage/Water Company of the Year Entrepreneurship and Social Impact Entrepreneur Man of the Year Entrepreneur Woman of the Year Not-for-Profit Organisation of the Year These categories are designed to recognise organisations and individuals that demonstrate exceptional performance, strong leadership, innovation and meaningful contributions to their respective sectors. In an increasingly competitive business environment, recognition can help distinguish a brand, strengthen its reputation and communicate its achievements to customers, partners, investors and other stakeholders. GBA offers businesses an opportunity to bring their accomplishments into the spotlight and celebrate the people, strategies and innovations behind their success. Participation can also create opportunities for networking, business engagement and greater visibility among industry leaders and other stakeholders. For entrepreneurs and corporate executives, the Awards provide a platform to celebrate leadership, inspire emerging businesses and demonstrate the value of building organisations that combine strong performance with long-term sustainability. Companies across eligible sectors are therefore encouraged to prepare their entries, showcase their achievements and take advantage of the opportunity to compete for recognition at the 2026 Awards. GBA 2026 also presents an opportunity for organisations seeking to strengthen their corporate visibility and align their brands with business excellence, innovation and national development.

items.title: Nouvelle attaque contre l’aéroport de Riyad : l’Algérie condamne une « agression odieuse »
items.description: L'Algérie a réagi ce dimanche à la nouvelle attaque perpétrée par les Houthis du Yémen contre l’aéroport international King Khalid de Riyad en Arabie saoudite qui a fait 12 morts et 300 blessés. « L'Algérie exprime sa ferme condamnation et sa profonde indignation suite au ciblage de l'aéroport international King Khalid de Riyad par des attaques ignobles qui ont coûté la vie à 12 civils, de nationalités saoudienne et étrangères, et fait plus de 300 blessés parmi les usagers et les employés de l'aéroport, en sus des dégâts matériels enregistrés », a déclaré le ministère des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué. Attaque contre l’aéroport de Riyad : l’Algérie dénonce une « agression odieuse » Pour l’Algérie, cette « agression odieuse » qui a visé cette infrastructure vitale et fait des victimes innocentes, constitue une « violation flagrante » de tous les usages internationaux, de la Charte des Nations Unies et du droit international humanitaire. Elle constitue aussi, ajoute le ministère des Affaires étrangères, une « atteinte grave » à la sécurité des civils et de la navigation aérienne garantie par les conventions internationales régissant l'aviation civile, ainsi qu'une « menace pour la sécurité et la stabilité régionale et internationale ». L'Algérie a réitéré, dans le même communiqué, « sa pleine solidarité avec le Royaume frère d'Arabie saoudite et exprime son rejet catégorique de tels agissements et de tout ce qui est de nature à porter atteinte à la souveraineté du Royaume, à l'intégrité de son territoire et à la sécurité de ses citoyens et résidents ». Mercredi, l’Autorité de l’aviation civile saoudienne a annoncé la mort de trois personnes dont une Algérienne dans deux attaques contre les aéroports de Riyad et d’Abha. L’article Nouvelle attaque contre l’aéroport de Riyad : l’Algérie condamne une « agression odieuse » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: T-bills auction: Demand improves as government exceeds target by about 76%; interest rates soften
items.description: Demand for treasury bills improved as the government exceeded its treasury bills target by about 76.4% to GH¢5.06 billion. This is coming despite some analysts’ prediction that investor interest will remain relatively soft at the next auction. The Treasury, however, accepted GH¢4.40 billion of the total bids as against a target of GH¢2.86 billion. According to auction results by the Bank of Ghana, the chunk of the bids came from the 91-day instrument. A little over GH¢3.2 billion of the bids were tendered, representing 64.9% of the total bids. The uptake was, however, GH¢3.0 billion. The 182-day bill received bids of about GH¢1.3 billion. A little above GH¢1.2 billion was accepted. For the 364-day bill, about GH¢468.9 million of the bids were tendered. A little above GH¢136.5 million of the bids were accepted. Meanwhile, interest rates continued to soften on the yield curve. This will help reduce the government’s cost of domestic debt. The yield on the 91-day bill declined by 4.0 basis points to 4.60%. That of the 182-day bill also went down to 6.27% from the previous week’6.31%. Similarly, the yield on the 364-day bill dropped by 5.0 basis points to 9.75%. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : une charte signée pour prévenir les abus sexuels sur les enfants
items.description: Le ministère de la Justice, le ministère du Tourisme et les acteurs du secteur touristique ont signé, samedi, une charte visant à prévenir les abus et l’exploitation sexuelle des enfants dans le cadre des voyages et du tourisme, à l’approche des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. La signature de cette charte s’inscrit dans une démarche préventive face à l’affluence touristique attendue au Sénégal lors de cet événement, dont Saly, dans le département de Mbour, fait partie des villes hôtes, indique une dépêche de l'APS. « L’objectif de cette charte, c’est vraiment de nous engager, d’identifier les responsabilités de chaque département, chaque structure, mais aussi chaque département ministériel », a expliqué le directeur des Droits humains, Julien Ngane Ndour, en marge d’une randonnée pédestre organisée à Saly dans le cadre d’une campagne de sensibilisation à la protection des enfants. Il a précisé que l’initiative ne vise pas à stigmatiser le secteur touristique, mais à mobiliser les professionnels et les institutions autour de la prévention des atteintes aux droits des enfants. De son côté, le directeur de la Réglementation touristique, Ndéné Ndao, a appelé les professionnels à signaler toute situation suspecte dans les hôtels, les agences de voyages et les autres espaces touristiques. « Le devoir de signalement et de vigilance incombe à tous les opérateurs », a-t-il déclaré, rappelant que la protection des enfants relève d’une responsabilité collective impliquant les institutions, les professionnels du tourisme, les communautés et les familles. Pour sa part, Aminata Kébé, experte en droits de l’homme et genre au Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies aux droits de l’homme et coordinatrice régionale du Projet d’appui à la protection des enfants victimes de violations de leurs droits (PAPEV), a indiqué que la randonnée faisait suite à deux journées de formation et d’échanges avec les acteurs locaux et régionaux ainsi que les organisations de la société civile. Elle a également insisté sur la coordination entre le Sénégal, la Guinée, la Guinée-Bissau et la Gambie, pays couverts par le projet PAPEV, afin d’harmoniser les actions de protection de l’enfance. La charte vise ainsi à clarifier les responsabilités des différents acteurs en matière de prévention, de sensibilisation et de protection des enfants à l’approche des JOJ Dakar 2026.

items.title: Après le choix de l’UC de rester hors du gouvernement, Ouzzine attend une offre de Mansouri
items.description: Après que l’Union constitutionnelle (UC) a choisi de rester en dehors du gouvernement et d’opter pour un soutien critique à la nouvelle équipe dirigée par Fatima Zahra Mansouri, coordinatrice du leadership collectif du Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), Mohammed Ouzzine, secrétaire général du Mouvement populaire (MP), a déclaré que son parti n’avait pas encore arrêté sa position. Il a également indiqué n’avoir reçu aucune nouvelle notification de la part de la nouvelle cheffe du gouvernement, chargée de former son équipe. Le Parti du mouvement démocratique et social devrait lui aussi rester en dehors de la coalition gouvernementale. Il devrait former, avec l’UC, un groupe parlementaire commun à la Chambre des représentants au cours de la législature ouverte vendredi dernier par le Roi Mohammed VI, suivant ainsi l’expérience de la précédente législature. Cette configuration placerait les deux formations hors de la participation gouvernementale. Dans une déclaration à Hespress , Ouzzine a souligné qu’ « aucun nouveau contact n’a eu lieu depuis la dernière réunion avec Mansouri ». Il a précisé qu’il n’avait alors reçu aucune proposition claire concernant une éventuelle participation au gouvernement. Le Mouvement populaire, a-t-il ajouté, « n’a demandé aucun portefeuille ministériel ni aucun poste institutionnel », estimant que le deuxième tour des consultations ne reposait pas sur une vision clairement définie de la part de la responsable chargée de former le gouvernement. À la lumière des derniers développements, marqués par le choix de l’UC d’apporter un soutien critique tout en préservant son indépendance politique, le secrétaire général du Mouvement populaire a affirmé que « la balle est dans le camp de Mansouri, et nulle part ailleurs » . Il a expliqué que son parti n’avait présenté aucune proposition de participation, dans l’attente d’une offre claire, une situation qui perdure malgré les nombreux changements intervenus. Hespress avait précédemment rapporté que, selon d’autres estimations, le Mouvement populaire resterait en dehors de la prochaine équipe gouvernementale si l’UC et le Parti du mouvement démocratique et social acceptaient d’apporter un soutien critique afin de renforcer la formule gouvernementale envisagée par Mansouri. Celle-ci réunirait le PAM, le Parti de l’Istiqlal, l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) et le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS). La configuration reste toutefois tributaire d’une annonce officielle de Mansouri et d’éventuels changements dans la première architecture de la coalition. Interrogé sur les 12 conseillers parlementaires dont dispose le Mouvement populaire et qui pourraient renforcer la majorité à la Chambre des conseillers, assurant ainsi une majorité dans les deux chambres du Parlement, Ouzzine a répondu : « C’est à la partie qui prend l’initiative de solliciter les autres de connaître les moyens dont dispose chaque partenaire pour assurer la réussite de la majorité. Ce n’est pas à la partie invitée aux consultations de dévoiler ses cartes. » « Jusqu’à présent, nous n’avons reçu aucun nouvel élément », a-t-il poursuivi. En l’absence de changement dans les prochaines heures, le Mouvement populaire, qui dispose de 29 sièges à la Chambre des représentants et constitue la cinquième force de cette institution, resterait donc dans l’expectative. Plusieurs indications laissent penser que le PAM, fort de ses 97 sièges, pourrait s’orienter vers une alliance avec les partis de la « Koutla démocratique ». La décision finale est attendue la semaine prochaine, selon une déclaration exclusive d’Abdelatif Ouahbi à Hespress. D’après les résultats officiels annoncés pour les circonscriptions locales et régionales, le Parti de l’Istiqlal dispose de 65 sièges, l’USFP de 26 et le PPS de 19, un total porté à 22 pour ce dernier à la faveur des alliances parlementaires récemment annoncées. Le scénario d’une coalition réunissant le PAM et ces trois formations totaliserait ainsi 210 sièges. La future « équipe Mansouri » pourrait également bénéficier du soutien critique du groupe parlementaire commun des deux partis, qui compte 25 députés. Selon les résultats des élections législatives de 2026 annoncés par le ministre de l’Intérieur le jeudi 24 septembre dernier, l’Union constitutionnelle a obtenu 17 sièges, tandis que le Parti du mouvement démocratique et social en a remporté huit. The post Après le choix de l’UC de rester hors du gouvernement, Ouzzine attend une offre de Mansouri appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Le 1er Joumada I de l'an 1448 de l'Hégire correspondra au mardi 13 octobre
items.description: Le 1er Joumada I de l'an 1448 de l'Hégire correspondra au mardi 13 octobre 2026, a annoncé dimanche le ministère des Habous et des Affaires islamiques. Dans un communiqué, le ministère indique avoir observé le croissant lunaire du mois de Joumada I ce dimanche 29 Rabii II 1448 de l'Hégire, correspondant au 11 octobre 2026, précisant avoir contacté les délégués des Affaires islamiques et les unités des Forces Armées Royales qui lui ont confirmé la non-observation du Croissant lunaire annonçant le début du mois de Joumada I. Ainsi, le mois de Rabii II aura compté 30 jours et le 1er Joumada I correspondra au mardi 13 octobre 2026, précise la même source. Puisse le Tout-Puissant, en ce mois béni, combler de ses bienfaits et de sa bénédiction SM le Roi Mohammed VI, Amir Al Mouminine, Protecteur de la patrie et de la religion, renouveler pareille occasion pour SAR le Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan et SAR le Prince Moulay Rachid ainsi que pour l’ensemble des membres de l'illustre Famille Royale dans le bonheur et les bienfaits, et accorder progrès et prospérité au peuple marocain et à toute la Oumma islamique, conclut le communiqué. items.title: Baladna Algérie dévoile de nouveaux chiffres sur sa ferme géante d’Adrar
items.description: Baladna El Djazaïr livre des chiffres sur l'évolution de son projet de ferme géante de 270 000 vaches à Adrar. Alors que les premières vaches américaines sont attendues pour fin novembre, les derniers chiffres dévoilés par l'entreprise sur les réseaux sociaux concernent notamment le nombre d'hectares emblavés et la production de la première récolte de céréales, le programme de la campagne en cours et les objectifs à terme. Voici la première production de céréales de la ferme Baladna Algérie Le projet intégré, fruit d'un investissement de 3,5 milliards de dollars entre le Fonds national d'investissement (FNI) et le qatari Baladna, porte sur la réalisation sur 219 000 hectares d’une méga ferme laitière de 270 000 vaches et d'une usine de production de poudre de lait d'une capacité de 193 000 tonnes par an. La production de la saison s’est élevée à 530 tonnes d'orge, 359 tonnes de blé, 584 tonnes de fourrages et 746 tonnes de maïs d’ensilage, alors que les surfaces emblavées étaient de 360 hectares, dont 210 hectares pour l’orge, 90 hectares pour le blé et 60 hectares pour le maïs d’ensilage, précise l’entreprise. Les rendements sont plutôt bons. Objectif 70 000 hectares et 1400 pivots d'irrigation Pour la campagne de labours-semailles 2026-2027, 420 hectares sont en cours d’emblavement, dont 360 hectares de maïs d’ensilage et 60 hectares de maïs supérieur, en plus de 550 hectares qui le seront incessamment, soit un total de 970 hectares supplémentaires. En outre, 11 pivots d’irrigation supplémentaires sont mis en service. L'objectif, indique Baladna El Djazaïr, est d'atteindre une surface emblavée de 70 000 hectares, irrigués par 1400 pivots. L’article Baladna Algérie dévoile de nouveaux chiffres sur sa ferme géante d’Adrar est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2023 Tinubu alliance failed to deliver national unity, competent govt – Makinde
items.description: By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has admitted that the political alliance he entered into with President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2023 general election failed to deliver the national unity, fairness and competent government he expected, declaring that he regrets supporting the President. Makinde said his decision to back Tinubu, then the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), was driven by the belief that the incoming administration would bring together capable Nigerians from different parts of the country to address the nation’s challenges, rather than govern along narrow political or regional lines. The governor made the disclosure during a live radio interview in Ibadan on Sunday, while revisiting the circumstances that led him and other aggrieved Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governors to support Tinubu instead of their party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the 2023 election. Explaining the motivation behind the alliance, Makinde said he had expected the President to prioritise the national interest, notwithstanding their different political affiliations and his lack of previous direct dealings with Tinubu. “I supported the current president, even though in another party at that time, because I thought, even though I never dealt directly with him, I thought we would do what is right for the country,” he said. Makinde said the expectation was that the administration would pursue national cohesion, fairness and equal opportunities, particularly after eight years of President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration, which he argued made the demand for a southern presidency a question of equity. He said his position was not merely about securing political advantage for himself or his allies but about ensuring that the country’s leadership reflected fairness and inclusion. “I supported fairness, justice and equity. I supported a united Nigeria, a Nigeria that gives opportunity to every part of this country,” the governor said. According to Makinde, the disagreements that culminated in the alliance with Tinubu arose from the PDP’s handling of its presidential candidacy and the party’s leadership structure ahead of the 2023 election. He said he and other aggrieved governors believed that the emergence of Atiku, a northerner, as the PDP’s presidential candidate, while Iyorchia Ayu, also from the North-Central, remained the party’s national chairman, did not adequately address their concerns about fairness and regional balance. “So, in 2023, we felt that after eight years of President Buhari who hailed from the north, the presidency should come to the south,” he said. Makinde disclosed that he initially supported the presidential ambition of the then Rivers State Governor, Nyesom Wike, within the PDP, but the party eventually settled for Atiku, deepening the disagreement between the party’s leadership and the group of governors who had demanded a different political arrangement. He said the group sought to resolve the dispute by persuading the PDP leadership to replace Ayu with Taofeek Arapaja, who was then the party’s Deputy National Chairman (South), as part of efforts to address the question of regional balance. Recounting a meeting with Atiku in London, Makinde said the request was straightforward: to allow the party to change its national chairman before proceeding with the election. “We met with him in London. The only thing I said to him in London was, allow us to go and remove Iyorchia Ayu and then make Taofeek Arapaja the acting chairman because he was the Deputy National Chairman (South) at that time,” he said. However, the disagreement remained unresolved, prompting the aggrieved governors to explore other political options ahead of the presidential election. Makinde said he eventually agreed to support Tinubu after an intermediary linked the group to the then APC presidential candidate, despite having no prior direct political dealings with him. “Because I had never had any political dealings with him (Tinubu) up until that point, someone else did the linking. I said, okay, fine. If this is what we will do, we will support you,” he said. The governor maintained that the understanding was based on expectations that a Tinubu-led administration would transcend party divisions and assemble a team capable of addressing Nigeria’s economic and governance challenges. He said he repeatedly made the expectations clear during the election campaign, stressing that the country needed a government built around competence and national unity. “But even as a candidate, I must have mentioned it three or four times that our expectation would be a government of national unity; a government of national competence where you could start the process of resetting this country,” Makinde said. However, assessing the administration against those expectations, the governor expressed dissatisfaction with what he described as a failure to establish the kind of inclusive and competence-driven government he had anticipated. “But is it what we are seeing right now? Is it a government of national competence? Is it a government of national unity? The answer is no,” he said. Makinde also recounted an episode involving a proposed ministerial appointment, saying Tinubu had asked him to recommend a candidate for a ministerial position. According to the governor, he submitted the name of an Oyo indigene whom he considered suitable for the position of Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, but the nominee was not appointed to the portfolio. Instead, Adebayo Adelabu, another Oyo-born politician, was appointed Minister of Power. Makinde said the episode contributed to his concerns about the political understanding between him and the President, although he maintained that his principal concern remained the quality and inclusiveness of governance at the national level. He further disclosed that Tinubu had indicated an interest in having him help organise the APC in Oyo State, an offer he rejected on the grounds that he remained a member of the PDP. Quoting his response to the President, Makinde said: “No, sir, I can never help you organise APC in Oyo State because I am of the PDP.” The governor’s latest remarks come against the backdrop of his subsequent decision to pursue his own presidential ambition, marking a significant shift from the alliance that helped shape the 2023 presidential contest. In May 2026, Makinde formally declared his presidential ambition under an alliance between the PDP and the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), presenting the arrangement as part of a broader effort to establish an alternative political platform. He has also argued that Nigeria requires a viable opposition to prevent the country from drifting towards a one-party state, maintaining that political differences should not eliminate democratic competition. Reiterating why he had supported Tinubu in 2023, Makinde said he had believed the President would bring together capable people from across the country to help address the nation’s problems and initiate a process of national renewal. “Reset the country, like I said, bring people from all over that can help the country. But unfortunately, that is not what we’re seeing. So I regret that action. Yes, I do,” he said. The governor also defended his decision to publicly acknowledge his regret, saying responsible leadership required the willingness to admit mistakes and apologise when necessary. He said no individual possessed complete knowledge of future events and that political decisions could sometimes produce outcomes different from those anticipated. “I’m also not afraid to apologise to people when I wrong them, because it’s only God that is all-knowing, that knows the end from the beginning,” Makinde said. The post 2023 Tinubu alliance failed to deliver national unity, competent govt – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ziope undertakes initiative to build a technologically inclined community, commissions self-help ICT lab
items.description: The Chiefs and people of Ziope in the Agotime Ziope District of the Volta Region have undertaken an initiative aimed at building a technologically inclined community. The initiative saw the commissioning of a well-equipped self-help information and communication technology lab for the community basic school, aimed at providing all-round training for pupils. This would enable the pupils to study the practical aspects of ICT, unlike previously, when they only had the theory with illustrations on the boards. The Ziope Community, under the leadership of Dufia, Togbe Kpoduave Ahiagba IV, instituted the Ngoryiza, 2024, to mobilise resources towards the development of the area. Noticing the significance of information and communication technology in today’s world, proceeds from the 2025 celebrations were directed at the construction of a lab. Community commitment At the commissioning ceremony, Togbe Kpoduave Ahiagba IV lauded the community’s enthusiasm towards initiatives aimed at enhancing the livelihoods of the residents. He identified their efforts towards the construction of a 4-unit nurses’ quarters to house staff posted to the community health centre, contributing to improved healthcare delivery in the area. He eulogised Rev Mensah Djokoto for providing forty desktop computers for the proposed ICT lab, which is furnished with an air conditioner, robotic logistics and an internet connection. “None of the public Junior High Schools in Ghana has this kind of logistics, as seen at the Ziope Basic School. I am happy we undertook this initiative to secure the future of our children and the Ziope community”, he said. Togbe Kpoduave Ahiagba IV urged them to continue to contribute towards such development initiatives, to drive development in the Ziope community. “In unity we will find strength and development. If you bring a cedi and I bring a cedi, doesn’t it become 2 cedis? Will your Cedi alone be able to do it? So we must continue on this agenda and not be tired as we have identified another project for next year”, he said. Coding and robotics Rev Mensah Djokoto explained that he was touched and took the decision with a friend to make such a significant contribution to the education of pupils in the community, in an attempt to give back to society. He said that a zeal to ensure the pupils have an all-round ICT education prompted him to add coding and robotics to the centre, hence involving the Ghana Code Club. The Founder and Director of Ghana Code Club, Ernestina Edem Appiah, said a practical curriculum beginning with digital literacy and computational thinking, artificial intelligence, coding, robotics and electronics will be deployed, targeting how to train the pupils in creating with technology. “The children will learn to build programs and animations using tools such as Scratch; they will explore critical computing with tools such as micro: bit. They will learn the foundations of robotics, and gradually be introduced to AI, including how AI works, how it can be used responsibly, and how they can use emerging texts to create solutions to problems within their own communities”, she said. “We strongly believe that coding begins in their minds. So even before a child becomes confident with her computer, we tell them how to think logically and identify patterns. Break problems into smaller parts, experiment, make mistakes, and try again. That is a kind of learning we want the centre to be present”, she added. BECE performance The Member of Parliament for Agotime Ziope, Charles Agvbeve, lauded the initiative, underscoring the need for communities to champion self-help projects, helping the government to develop the country. He expressed optimism about performance in the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) would improve as the “Agotime Ziope District scored first in 2025”, urging pupils of the final year students of the Ziope Basic School to score 1 in ICT in the 2026 BECE. He advised that the ICT lab should be used as a learning centre for pupils from other schools in the enclave to enhance their training as well. The Volta Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress, Mawutor Agbavitor, was elated with the initiative, acknowledging their efforts to lead the way in developing their community. He was enthused with their choice of enhancing ICT training of the pupils, as ”ICT is no longer a luxury but rather a necessity. The jobs of tomorrow, the knowledge of today, and the competition our children will face, all require digital skills.” The community launched the 2027 edition of the Ngoryiza, hoping to raise funds to tackle other social needs of the community.

items.title: Authorities impose Section 144 in Karachi, ban gatherings of more than 5 people till Oct 20
items.description: KARACHI: The Karachi commissioner on Sunday imposed Section 144 in the metropolis till Oct 20 to prevent protests and demonstrations from inconveniencing the public and causing a “deterioration of the law and order situation”. Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons. The notification, issued by Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi, said that it had been reported that protests, demonstrations, sit-ins and rallies were being held on major roads, junctions and roundabouts, causing severe traffic congestion and posing “serious security concerns”. “Such road blockages are disrupting routine public life, impeding the movement of emergency services and restricting access to hospitals. Accordingly, it has been requested that a ban under Section 144 of the CrPC be imposed on protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies and assemblies of more than five persons within the territorial limits of Karachi Division,” it said. The notification said that there was “reasonable apprehension” that the holding, organising or facilitating of such gatherings, rallies, protests, demonstrations, processions and assemblies may “obstruct public roads and thoroughfares, disrupt normal civic and commercial activities, cause inconvenience to the general public and traffic congestion, impede access to hospitals, and result in untoward incidents and the deterioration of the law and order situation”. It said that it was considered “necessary and expedient” to impose preventive restrictions for a specified period to avert any possible untoward incident, maintain public peace and tranquillity, safeguard the lives and property of citizens, ensure public safety and security, and facilitate the uninterrupted movement of the general public and essential services. Therefore, the Karachi commissioner prohibited holding, organising, convening, facilitating or participating in protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies, processions or other public gatherings involving more than five persons from Oct 11 (Sunday) to Oct 20.

items.title: Burkina Faso: Samedi noir pour Kenzy Bationo de L’As du Lycée, victime d’un grave accident
items.description: Selon les informations révélées par l’influenceuse Aïcha la Battante, l’acteur burkinabè Kenzy Bationo, célèbre interprète du personnage de « Joe » dans la série culte L’As du Lycée , a été victime d’un grave accident de la circulation dans la nuit du samedi 10 au dimanche 11 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. C’est une nouvelle fois Aïcha la Battante, déjà au cœur de la chaîne de solidarité ayant permis son évacuation sanitaire au Maroc au début de l'année, qui a donné l'alerte sur son état de santé critique et engagé les premières démarches pour sa prise en charge médicale d'urgence. L’émotion est vive au sein du monde culturel et chez les amoureux du 7e art burkinabè. Dans la nuit du samedi 10 au dimanche 11 octobre 2026, aux environs de 23 h 50, l’acteur Kenzy Bationo a été impliqué dans un violent accident de la circulation à Ouagadougou. L’information a été rendue publique par l'activiste et influenceuse Aïcha la Battante, avant d'être confirmée. Transporté d’urgence vers les services de santé de la capitale, le comédien se trouve dans un état jugé préoccupant, nécessitant une mobilisation médicale immédiate. Ce drame intervient alors que Kenzy Bationo venait à peine de retrouver le chemin de la dignité. Après un premier accident en 2022 ayant altéré son apparence et l'ayant plongé dans la précarité et l'addiction dans les rues de Ouagadougou, une immense vague de solidarité nationale s'était organisée. En mars 2026, grâce à une cagnotte initiée par Aïcha la Battante, le comédien avait pu bénéficier d'un vol médicalisé vers le Maroc pour une cure de désintoxication et des soins intensifs de quatre mois. Son retour au pays, célébré le 8 juillet 2026, laissait espérer une réintégration sociale et artistique définitive. Ce tragique accident de la route replonge brusquement l'interprète de « Joe » et ses admirateurs dans l'épreuve. Sur les réseaux sociaux et dans les milieux artistiques, les messages de soutien et les appels à la prière se multiplient pour accompagner l'acteur et saluer le dévouement continu d'Aïcha la Battante. La rédaction de [lien suspect supprimé] reste attentive à l'évolution de son état de santé et aux démarches d'évacuation médicale en cours. items.title: ECG announces power outage in parts of Tema, Central Region due to network fault, maintenance
items.description: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced a power outage affecting parts of the Tema Region due to a fault in its network, while several communities in the Central Region will experience a temporary interruption in electricity supply on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, to allow for planned maintenance works. In a notice to customers, ECG’s Tema Region said the network fault had affected Comm. 17, Timber Market, Resolve Hospital, Bakeshop, Marina Mall at Spintex, Baatsonaa and surrounding areas. The company said its engineers were working to resolve the fault and restore electricity supply to the affected communities. ECG apologised to customers for the inconvenience caused by the unplanned outage and assured them that efforts were underway to address the problem. The company did not specify when power supply would be fully restored to the affected areas. Meanwhile, ECG has scheduled planned maintenance works for Tuesday, October 13, from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., which will result in a temporary power outage in several communities, mainly in the Central Region. The affected areas include Komenda, Kissi, Ayensudo, Ampenyi, Elmina, Eguafo, Aburansa, Besease, Ebu Krom, Agona Town, Breman, Iture, Duakro, Amamuma, and surrounding communities, as well as several other towns and settlements listed in the company’s notice. The company said the maintenance exercise forms part of efforts to improve service delivery and apologised in advance for the inconvenience customers may experience. ECG has urged affected customers to take note of the scheduled outage and make the necessary preparations ahead of the exercise.
