items.title: Pakistan Army deployed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in aid of civil power
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after imposing an emergency and governor’s rule in the province. The authorisation of the army deployment was made through Statutory Regulatory Order, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday. According to the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the “safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations” in the province. The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added. Copies of the order were forwarded to the president’s secretary, prime minister’s adviser, the KP governor’s secretary, the Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, the KP home secretary, the inspector general of police (IGP) in the province, the Peshawar High Court registrar and other officials. The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation. That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks . Police guard a road leading to Red Zone, in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations. On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. Shipping containers block roads Shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block roads after the imposition of the emergency. Containers were placed near Peshawar’s railway station to block the routes towards Khyber Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and beyond. They were also placed near Edwardes College to block entry to Jail Road and Malik Saad Shaheed Flyover, while people were turned away from Sher Shah Suri Road as it was reported to be completely closed. Police were reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House. The deployment included personnel called from other districts. Police and personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including many in plainclothes, were seen patrolling the roads leading to Governor House, the central police office, Peshawar police headquarters and other government installations largely located in the Red Zone, a correspondent reported. Vehicles with tinted glasses, police mobile vans, armored personnel carriers and other LEA vehicles were reportedly the only transport visible in and around the cantonment area, with life at a standstill and the area appearing deserted. Another correspondent reported that the road leading to Khyber Road was shuttered by a container and the traffic control gate closed. A large number of police personnel were also seen around Surey Pul, a favoured spot for protesters. Grand Trunk (GT) Road was blocked by containers at Firdous Chowk and the correspondent reported a large number of police personnel in the area. Only pedestrians were allowed to move ahead. Additionally, containers near Bala Hisar Fort and outside the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) office on Arbab Road blocked entry towards Mall Road. A vehicle moves past a shipping container used to block a road leading to the Red Zone, in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters Only official vehicles were being allowed to travel from Governor House towards the Chief Minister’s House, while tight security was reported on Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum road where they are located. The Civil Secretariat was seen to be deserted. Royal Artillery (RA) Bazaar has been closed, while Saddar remains partially open. Additionally, Peshawar’s Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) stations were reported to be shuttered by Dawn ’s correspondent. The stretch of Khyber Road connecting to University Road and Airport Road at Aman Chowk was reported to be open but with low traffic. A large police contingent was seen at Aman Chowk. Meanwhile, University Road was blocked by containers at Tehkal, and containers at Stadium Chowk allowed for only single-file passage of vehicles on both sides. Earlier, traffic jams were reported due to the closure of Khyber Road, which connects GT Road with the eastern side of University Road and serves as the main artery and choke point. The resulting diversions created pressure on auxiliary roads. The area is part of the cantonment, and the Red Zone contains important installations such as the Corps Commander’s House, civil secretariat, central police office, CM Secretariat, CM House and Governor House. All telecoms services, including landline and DSL, are reported to be suspended in the provincial capital. The city had witnessed a nearly 48-hour mobile service blackout just days ago, on account of the presence of the PTI in the city for its long march . With networks suspended, people faced immense issues in withdrawing money from bank accounts, as ATMs remained out of service for the entire day. Aside from the suspension of cellular network and broadband services, however, the situation remained normal for those living on Kohat Road, Charsadda Road, GT Road beyond Pir Zakorhi Bridge, and the area bordering the Khyber district, as well as others on the outskirts of the provincial capital. Vehicles of the armed forces were also reported to be patrolling cantonment areas and a heavy deployment of police was reported in both the city and its outskirts including Kohat Road, GT Road, University Road and Warsak Road. Separately, a holiday has been declared for schools, colleges and universities in the district on Monday (Oct 12), according to a notification issued by the deputy commissioner of Peshawar. “It is hereby notified that all educational institutions, both public and private, including schools, colleges and universities, shall remain closed on October 12, 2026 (Monday) located within the territorial jurisdiction of District Peshawar,” the notification said. On Saturday, KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed put district police on alert for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force. Police personnel stand guard near shipping containers blocking a road leading to the Red Zone in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters A notification issued by the IGP’s office directed not only officers in Peshawar but also district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and even station house officers (SHOs) to personally monitor the situation. It said DPOs could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action. It added that the use of force was to be carried out on a gradated basis, noting that in the first phase, protesters should be clearly warned against violence before police began to use forceful measures.

items.title: Algérie : 61 Marocains qui « préparaient des actes de sabotage » arrêtés
items.description: Des ressortissants marocains qui « préparaient des actes de sabotage » en Algérie ont été arrêtés à Oran début octobre, a annoncé ce dimanche 11 octobre la Direction générale de la sûreté nationale. La même source a indiqué que la police a démantelé un « réseau criminel international marocain dont les membres opéraient sur le territoire national, avec l'arrestation de 61 ressortissants marocains qui s'apprêtaient à commettre des actes de sabotage portant atteinte à la sécurité et à l'ordre publics . » Les enquêtes préliminaires ont révélé que les membres de ce réseau criminel organisé, considéré comme « extrêmement dangereux » , « planifiaient l'exécution d'actes de sabotage » en Algérie, a ajouté la DGSN. Les 61 Marocains arrêtés à Oran se sont infiltrés en Algérie via la Tunisie Les arrestations ont eu lieu à Oran début octobre où la police a « réussi à déjouer ce plan criminel et à interpeller 61 Marocains — dont un ancien militaire de l'armée marocaine », a précisé la même source. Les ressortissants marocains arrêtés à Oran se sont introduits illégalement en Algérie via la Tunisie. Arrivés par avion à Tunis, ils ont emprunté des « sentiers montagneux escarpés et des passages forestiers isolés dans la région d'El Kala (wilaya d'El Tarf), limitrophe de la frontière tunisienne, avant de se rendre par voie terrestre à Oran pour préparer la mise à exécution de leurs plans de sabotage », a détaillé la DGSN. Menée sous la supervision du parquet compétent, cette opération a également permis la « saisie de passeports marocains ainsi que de sommes d'argent en dirhams marocains et en euros ». Les suspects ont été déférés devant le procureur de la République près le pôle pénal spécialisé d'Oran. L’article Algérie : 61 Marocains qui « préparaient des actes de sabotage » arrêtés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: TTAP condemns imposition of governor’s rule, emergency in KP, calls move 'unconstitutional'
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Sunday condemned the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming the move unconstitutional and contrary to democratic principles. It announced that it would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums. It also said the long march would go ahead as planned. Addressing a press conference, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said governor’s rule and an emergency would not resolve the province’s problems, stressing that counterterrorism efforts required a unified strategy developed through political consensus. He rejected allegations that the KP government had failed to cooperate with the federal government in tackling terrorism, saying the provincial administration remained committed to eliminating the menace. “If the problem of terrorism exists in 12 districts, why has governor’s rule been imposed across the province?” he asked. Gohar said the PTI had consistently condemned terrorism in all its forms and maintained that the country’s security and defence remained paramount. However, he argued that counterterrorism measures should not be used to justify action against his party. He said the PTI would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums, adding that the party’s struggle for constitutional and democratic rights would continue. The PTI chairman also called for the release of political prisoners and the restoration of the legal rights of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. He demanded that Imran be transferred to a hospital for treatment, that his family be allowed to meet him, and that details of his health and treatment be shared with them. Gohar said the party had approached the Supreme Court and high courts 19 times seeking relief for its incarcerated founder. He said the announcement of a long march for Aug 5 had been made to secure Imran’s rights after the party failed to obtain relief through the courts. He claimed that around 1,500 PTI workers were imprisoned in Punjab, while 10 members of the provincial assembly, including three ministers, and eight members of the National Assembly had also been arrested. The PTI chairman rejected the government’s narrative about his party, arguing that political action against the PTI should not be linked to efforts to eliminate terrorism. He further claimed that terrorism had not been discussed during 15 meetings with government representatives before Oct 2. He said the KP government had increased police capacity, provided security resources and participated in counterterrorism meetings. Gohar said federal interference had weakened the provincial government’s authority, adding that sidelining an elected chief minister was inconsistent with democratic principles. Consensus needed on counterterrorism PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party had consistently called for a mutually agreed strategy to address terrorism, arguing that decisions on security operations should be taken in consultation with all political parties. Referring to the Parachinar agreement, he said the party’s position had remained clear and that it was seeking the implementation of previously agreed decisions rather than the introduction of new conditions. He said the party had cited the February 2026 meeting of the Apex Committee and a resolution adopted at a peace jirga as the basis for moving forward. Raja said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had taken a clear position and that the provincial government could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to undertake whatever measures it considered appropriate. “We cannot give anyone written permission to do whatever they want and then endorse it,” he said. He added that any decision concerning governor’s rule or an emergency must be made in accordance with constitutional principles and political consensus. Raja said negotiations had involved consultations with Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, while Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other political leaders had been trying to ensure the process succeeded. He claimed that the talks had been progressing satisfactorily and that the imposition of an emergency was a hasty decision. He also cited Senator Kamran Murtaza as saying that negotiations were moving in the right direction. The TTAP leader described the arrest of a provincial assembly speaker as an extraordinary step, adding that the assembly remained in existence. Despite what he described as a crackdown on the PTI, Raja said the party remained committed to its principles and was seeking peace and protection for innocent people. He confirmed that there had been no change to the announcement of the long march by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying peaceful protest was a fundamental constitutional right. “We will not throw stones. Through peaceful protest, we have to express our moral position,” he said, adding that a large-scale, peaceful demonstration by citizens across the country would convey a strong message. He said people would decide how to express their displeasure over what he described as actions against democracy, while distinguishing between political protest and revolutionary action. National Action Plan must be implemented Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said Pakistan was a federation whose provinces were united under a single Constitution, and criticised the treatment meted out to the PTI. He claimed that Imran had received the majority of public support in the elections and alleged that the ruling establishment feared the public mandate and had continuously targeted the PTI. Abbas blamed the government for the prevailing insecurity, saying the conduct of those in power had caused greater damage than the country’s external enemies could inflict. He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and said the seven days since the start of negotiations could have been used to make progress towards a political settlement. Abbas further said the party could not support military operations in which ordinary citizens became victims, stressing that counterterrorism measures must protect civilians and contribute to lasting peace. The press conference was held at an imambargah in Islamabad’s Bhara Kahu as the KP House, where the alliance would typically hold press conferences had been sealed. Speaking to Dawn , TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed. He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee. “Then we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.

items.title: JoyNews’ Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah selected for UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technologies Fellowship
items.description: JoyNews journalist and digital content creator Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah has been selected for the UK Media Excellence for Emerging Technologies (UK MEET) Fellowship, a programme designed to strengthen journalists’ ability to report on emerging technologies and their impact on society. The fellowship, delivered by Imperial College London through Imperial Global Ghana with support from the British High Commission, brings together journalists to engage with researchers, examine technological claims and develop evidence-led stories on science, technology and innovation. Jacqueline was selected from a pool of more than 500 applicants from Ghana and Nigeria, with approximately 13 per cent of applicants accepted into the programme. The residential programme, running from October 11 to 17, 2026, in Accra, focuses on helping journalists interrogate claims about emerging technologies, assess evidence and communicate complex scientific developments in ways that are accessible and relevant to the public. For Jacqueline, the fellowship presents an opportunity to strengthen her reporting on artificial intelligence and its growing influence on public life, particularly education. One of her proposed investigations examines whether AI-powered learning tools being introduced into Ghana’s Senior High School education system are improving learning outcomes and whether students across different communities are benefiting equally. The proposed story seeks to move beyond claims about the potential of artificial intelligence to examine what the evidence shows about its performance in classrooms, how teachers and students use the tools, and whether differences in access to devices, connectivity and digital support affect the benefits students receive. The investigation would draw on the experiences of students and teachers, alongside insights from independent researchers, technology developers and education authorities. Yeboah’s approach reflects a central question in technology reporting: how can journalists independently test claims about innovation and explain what the findings mean for the people expected to use it? The fellowship also provides opportunities for journalists to collaborate with researchers and fellow media professionals, develop story ideas and explore how emerging technologies can be reported responsibly. As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly prominent in education, healthcare and other sectors, evidence-led journalism will be important in helping the public understand both the opportunities and limitations of these technologies. Jacqueline Ansomah Yeboah is a journalist and digital content creator with JoyNews, where she works on public-interest reporting, digital storytelling and explainers. Jacqueline is among five JoyNews journalists selected for the programme. The others are Clinton Yeboah, Esther Nkrumah, Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom, Blessed Sogah and Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen. In all, 30 Ghanaians were selected for the programme.

items.title: 'Our fight is against terrorism': Kundi chairs first meeting of KP Advisory Council
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday chaired the first meeting of the KP Advisory Council, which was formed by the federal government following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in the province. At the outset of the meeting, all members of the council introduced themselves and their portfolios. Addressing the meeting, Kundi congratulated the members of the council, while noting that they would have to face many challenges. He said that they would get a briefing on the portfolios they had been assigned and would get a few days to familiarise themselves. “We have to fast-track things. There will be zero tolerance on corruption. Things should be done in a timely manner,” he said, adding that they would have to demonstrate a clear difference from the work done by their predecessors. He said that the first order of business was the law and order situation, adding that there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces. He said that the current situation was an “opportunity” as he called for building the province’s soft image. “If we have peace, we will get tourists and investors. My support is with you. I am available for you 24/7,” he said. Kundi then went on to read out a message for the people of the province, in which he said that due to “extraordinary circumstances”, “necessary measures” were taken under the Constitution. He said that he would refrain from levelling allegations and political rhetoric. “I have one message: peace, protection and stability have to be brought back to KP,” he said. He added that the people of KP had paid a huge price for the terrorism that plagued the province. “The time has now come to give the people of the province, who have rendered these sacrifices, the right to peace. Our fight is against terrorism. Our fight is against the ideology and network which facilitates terrorism and weakens the implementation of the law,” he said. He also said that Pakhtuns were not a cause of terrorism, but were the “biggest victims”. Therefore, the state had resolved that terrorism would be eliminated from KP and the people would be allowed to live their lives without fear. “My first priority will be protecting the peace and the people. Right now, our biggest priority is taking effective steps against terrorism. For this, the capacity of the police and the Counter Terrorism Department will be increased,” he said. He went on to say that another objective would be to cater to the people. “Mere statements are not the real test of a government, rather the service it provides to the people,” he said. Kundi said that the council would focus on healthcare, education and employment. The last objective, he said, would be to eliminate the whole ecosystem giving rise to terrorism in the province. “We cannot solve the issue by just targeting terrorists. Those facilitating and financing … must be eliminated,” he said, adding that those involved in terrorism would be dealt with according to the law. He assured the people of KP that the “extraordinary steps” taken were not meant to target a particular party or group. Kundi said that the main purpose was to ensure peace and security as he asked for their cooperation. Security situation reviewed Separately, Kundi chaired a high-level meeting regarding the security situation in the province, during which he was briefed in detail on the overall situation, counter-terrorism efforts and the current circumstances. According to a handout, it was decided during the meeting that all containers currently placed in Peshawar will be removed in phases “as soon as possible”. “Internet services will be partially restored based on necessity,” the statement added. It was also decided during the meeting to enhance the compensation package for martyred police personnel and to review police salaries, as well as to pay “special attention” to the education and training of the heirs of martyred personnel. The governor commended the role of the administration and the police, remarking that it was a “positive development” that no untoward incident had occurred amid the prevailing circumstances, the handout said. He added that eradicating terrorism was a “top priority” and that the operational capacity of the police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) would be further improved to achieve this goal. “The meeting was attended by Advisor on Home Affairs Kifayatullah Khan, Chief Secretary Dr Muhammad Fakhr-e-Alam Irfan, Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Amjad Ali Khan, Additional IG Special Branch Muhammad Kashif Alam, Additional IG CTD, CCPO Dr Mian Saeed, Joint Director General IB Arshad Ali Khan, and other relevant officials,” the statement added.

items.title: Otti warns Abians against selling future for ₦5,000, rice
items.description: — Says politicians who ruined state over 24 years are back By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has warned voters against trading the state’s future for paltry financial inducements ahead of the 2027 general elections, cautioning that accepting as little as ₦5,000, ₦10,000, rice or wrappers from politicians could mortgage the state’s destiny for another four years. Otti, who spoke on Sunday through his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, at the Second Session of the Seventh Synod of the Anglican Communion, Aba Ngwa North Diocese, alleged that politicians responsible for Abia’s 24 years of underdevelopment were returning to seek the people’s support. He urged voters to scrutinise the records and intentions of politicians rather than allow temporary material benefits to influence their choices at the polls. The synod, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi, Umuocham, Aba, had the theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts 17:11-12. Warning that the consequences of selling votes could outlast the immediate benefits, Otti said, “Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years. Even prayer and fasting will not open it.” He added, “May we not lose what God has given to us on a platter of gold.” The governor also cautioned Christians against being swayed by politicians who, according to him, had suddenly become attentive to the church and its members as the election season approached. “Many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church. Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said. Otti urged the electorate to examine such political overtures critically and make informed decisions about the state’s future. ‘Next four years for consolidation’ The governor said his administration had spent its first three years laying the foundation for Abia’s development, expressing confidence that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would focus on consolidating the gains recorded so far. “Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins,” he said. According to him, the next phase would bring consolidation and further development, adding that Abia had become a point of reference. On the church’s development projects, Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support while reiterating that public funds must be deployed for the overall development of the state rather than individual religious projects. He also urged Christians to verify information and think critically before reaching conclusions, saying the church had an important role to play in changing the country’s negative narratives. “Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation, and especially our state,” he said. Church leaders preach political discernment Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Rt. Rev. Dr Nathan Kanu, said the synod’s theme challenged Christians to move beyond merely hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely. Kanu commended Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities. He also presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings upon the governor and his administration. In his sermon, the guest speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Rt. Rev. Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to examine what they hear before taking action. Speaking on “The Bereans’ Wisdom,” with texts from Acts 17:12-15, Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was particularly relevant in the present circumstances. “It didn’t say throw it away; it says think through it,” he said, regretting that some Christians had become vulnerable to deception because they failed to examine issues in the light of biblical teachings. “When members of the church know the Bible, they would not be deceived,” he added. The cleric also thanked God for giving Abia Governor Otti, whom he credited with changing the state’s narrative. items.title: 2027: Atiku demands names of firms printing INEC’s ballot papers
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disclose who is printing sensitive materials for the 2027 elections, warning that opaque contracts and key departmental redeployments could undermine confidence in the polls. His central concern is that Nigerians could head into a decisive election without knowing who is producing their ballots, how the contracts were awarded or what safeguards exist against political interference. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, for the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded explanations for reported changes in INEC’s Electoral Operations Department and allegations that a substantial share of sensitive election materials had been allocated to private contractors. Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gum was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode was also identified as head of Information and Communication Technology. “These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference.” Atiku also demanded that INEC confirm or deny whether Hitech, or any company associated with it, had secured a contract to print sensitive election materials. He alleged that more than half of the materials, including presidential ballot assets, might have been allocated to an undisclosed company believed to be based in France. He further questioned reports that the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Plc was printing materials for only 15 to 17 states, leaving private firms to handle the remainder. “Nigerians should not have to depend on unnamed sources to discover who is producing their ballots,” he said, demanding the disclosure of contractors, allocations, procurement methods and security arrangements. Atiku argued that any contract awarded to Hitech or an associated company would raise questions about INEC’s neutrality, citing publicly reported business ties between the Chagoury family, which owns Hitech, and the Tinubu family. The former vice-president also pointed to controversy surrounding Hitech contracts under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, including the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway project. “If neither Hitech nor a company associated with it has been selected, INEC must say so clearly and put the matter beyond doubt,” he said. He urged the Central Bank of Nigeria to disclose its banknote-printing allocations and explain the roles of domestic and foreign contractors, while calling on INEC to maximise domestic security-printing capacity and ensure every ballot and result sheet is protected by a transparent chain of custody. Atiku warned that Nigerians battered by economic hardship would resist any attempt to subvert their votes, insisting that the 2027 election must not become an instrument for prolonging the Tinubu administration’s hold on power. “Let there be no mistake: Nigerians will not accept a stolen election. Any attempt to rig the 2027 polls will be met with determined resistance through the ballot, lawful civic action, and every other democratic channel available to the people.” He said the ADC would monitor INEC’s preparations and alert domestic and international observers to any lack of transparency, insisting that the commission must prove its impartiality through verifiable disclosures. items.title: Liga : Ezzalzouli buteur dans le large succès du Real Betis face à Osasuna
items.description: L’international marocain Abdessamad Ezzalzouli a contribué dimanche au large succès du Real Betis face à Osasuna (5-2), en inscrivant un but lors de cette rencontre comptant pour la 8e journée du championnat espagnol de football. Titulaire, l’attaquant des Lions de l’Atlas a trouvé le chemin des filets à la 31e minute, permettant aux Andalous de porter leur avance à 2-0 au stade La Cartuja. Il signe ainsi sa deuxième réalisation de la saison en LaLiga. Le Real Betis avait ouvert le score dès la 10e minute grâce à Isco Alarcón, sur penalty, avant qu’Ezzalzouli ne double la mise. Osasuna a réduit l’écart par Ante Budimir (51e), puis par Raúl García de Haro (56e), relançant brièvement la rencontre. Isco a ensuite inscrit son deuxième but personnel à la 67e minute, avant que José Antonio Morante ne scelle la victoire des Andalous dans le temps additionnel (90e+6). À l’issue de cette rencontre, le Real Betis occupe la troisième place du classement avec 19 points, tandis qu’Osasuna se positionne au 15e rang avec 8 unités. items.title: Mental Health Alliance urges government to operationalise Mental Health Fund
items.description: The Ghana Alliance for Mental Health and Development has called on the government to operationalise the Mental Health Fund established under Section 82 of the Mental Health Act, 2012 (Act 846), to improve the financing of mental healthcare in the country. The Fund was established to provide sustainable financing for mental healthcare delivery, improve psychiatric infrastructure, support mental health research and promote the welfare of patients and healthcare workers. However, the Alliance says the Fund has remained dormant since its establishment in 2012, despite the growing need for investment in mental health services. It is urging the government and relevant stakeholders to take urgent steps to activate the Fund, arguing that the country’s mental healthcare system is facing significant challenges. The Alliance believes operationalising the Fund would provide a sustainable source of financing for mental healthcare delivery and strengthen efforts to address mental health challenges. The call was contained in a communiqué signed by Peter Badimak Yaro, National Convenor of the Ghana Alliance for Mental Health and Development, to commemorate World Mental Health Day 2026, under the theme “Lived Experiences Heard, Real Voices, Real Change”. “While the Mental Health Alliance commends the Government of Ghana for including four mental health conditions on the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), we call on the government to significantly improve financing for mental health through actualising the Mental Health Fund and adequately resourcing it through domestic resource mobilisation. Doing this will bring about full implementation of the Mental Health Law”, the communiqué stated. Alliance proposes 5% employment quota for persons with disabilities The Alliance has also proposed that the government reserve a 5% employment quota in local government institutions for persons with disabilities. It said the proposed policy should be supported by clear implementation and monitoring procedures to ensure that eligible persons benefit. The Alliance further called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to ensure that the 5% allocation of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) is used effectively to equip beneficiaries, including persons with physical, mental and psychosocial disabilities, with employable skills and support for income-generating activities. “Similarly, we call for increased employment of persons with disabilities, especially young people and females in the corporate and private sectors. These will be realised if the Ghana Labour Law and Disability Law are fully implemented”, the Alliance stressed. Call to end stigma and discrimination The Alliance called for increased advocacy by stakeholders to eliminate social stigma, prejudice, stereotypes and discrimination against persons with disabilities. It also urged stakeholders to promote the participation of persons with disabilities and those who have recovered from mental health conditions in socioeconomic, civic and political activities. “In particular, people with disabilities and lived experience of mental health conditions must be included as key decision-makers in designing programmes and services planned to support them”, the communiqué stated. The Alliance stressed that people with disabilities and those with lived experience of mental health conditions should have a meaningful role in shaping the policies and services intended to support them. Alliance urges responsible media reporting and public accountability The Alliance said the media had a special responsibility to educate the public about mental health and disability while helping to combat stigma. It urged media practitioners to use respectful language and protect the dignity and privacy of persons with lived experience of mental health conditions. It also appealed to journalists to avoid sensationalism and adopt responsible, rights-based reporting on disability and mental health issues. The Alliance proposed partnerships between the media and civil society organisations to produce educational materials and organise campaigns to promote inclusion and challenge stigma. “Partnerships with civil society and the Creative Industry could support documentaries, short films and public education campaigns that challenge stigma, and hold institutions accountable for their commitments”, the Alliance stated. Alliance calls for measurable results The Alliance called on the Ministry of Finance, the Administrator of the DACF and MMDAs to strengthen transparency and accountability in disability-related funding. It also urged relevant local government institutions to operationalise inclusive employment measures to improve access to jobs and economic opportunities for persons with disabilities. National planning and employment agencies, it said, should integrate disability and mental health inclusion into development programmes. Development partners, foundations and private businesses were also encouraged to invest in inclusive employment, community-based mental health services, legal accountability and sustained anti-stigma campaigns. “We cannot continue to celebrate commitments while people remain excluded from jobs, essential services and decisions that affect their lives. Inclusion must be reflected in budgets, employment opportunities, accessible services and measurable results,” the Mental Health Alliance stated. The Alliance reiterated that persons with disabilities and those with lived experience of mental health conditions must not merely be consulted but must meaningfully influence the policies, programmes and resources designed to support them.

items.title: Trump annonce une trêve énergétique immédiate entre la Russie et l’Ukraine, Moscou ne confirme pas l’accord et Zelensky se dit prêt à l’accepter
items.description: Le president americain Donald Trump a annonce ce 11 octobre sur Truth Social l'entree en vigueur immediate d'un cessez-le-feu energetique entre la Russie et l'Ukraine. Selon lui, Moscou et Kiev auraient accepte de suspendre les frappes visant les infrastructures energetiques des deux pays. « Un cessez-le-feu energetique entre immediatement en vigueur dans la guerre entre la Russie et l'Ukraine. Les deux parties ont donne leur accord. Ne le violez pas ! », a ecrit Donald Trump, sans preciser les conditions de mise en œuvre de cette mesure. En Russie, aucune confirmation d'un tel accord ne ressort des declarations. Le vice-president de la commission de l'energie de la Douma d'etat, Igor Ananskikh, a indique ne disposer d'aucune information concernant une eventuelle treve energetique avec l'Ukraine. Le parlementaire a egalement estime que Donald Trump faisait regulierement ce type d'annonces afin d'eviter une hausse des prix du petrole. Zelensky surpris par l'annonce, mais pret a accepter la treve a Kiev, l'annonce americaine a suscite la surprise. Un haut responsable proche de Volodymyr Zelensky a indique que les autorites ukrainiennes n'avaient pas connaissance d'un accord conclu avec Moscou sur la suspension des frappes contre les installations energetiques. Zelensky a lui-meme reconnu sa surprise. « L'annonce du cessez-le-feu a ete une surprise pour moi », a-t-il declare, precisant que l'Ukraine etait disposee a accepter une treve energetique si la Russie y consentait egalement. Zelensky a par ailleurs demande des precisions sur les eventuelles discussions entre les presidents russe et americain. « Si le president Trump a negocie cela avec Poutine, veuillez nous dire quand le cessez-le-feu commence. Nous sommes prets et nous l'accepterons », a-t-il dit. Dans une declaration ulterieure, le dirigeant ukrainien a qualifie cette initiative de « bonne nouvelle », tout en soulignant la necessite qu'elle « devienne une realite ». Il a egalement assure que les forces armees ukrainiennes avaient recu les instructions necessaires. Moscou avait deja reaffirme son ouverture aux negociations Sur le plan diplomatique, le Kremlin avait rappele, avant l'annonce de Trump, que la Russie demeurait ouverte a la poursuite des negociations sur le reglement du conflit ukrainien. Le porte-parole du president russe, Dmitri Peskov, avait egalement ete interroge sur l'eventualite de conditionner la reprise des pourparlers a l'organisation d'elections en Ukraine. Il avait precise que Vladimir Poutine ne s'etait pas encore exprime sur cette question.

items.title: Ghana–Holy See agreement heads to Parliament after Cabinet approval
items.description: Cabinet has approved a longstanding Host Country Agreement between Ghana and the Holy See, clearing the way for its submission to Parliament for ratification. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced the decision on Friday, October 9, 2026, during a meeting with the Apostolic Nuncio to Ghana, Archbishop Julien Kaboré. The agreement seeks to set out the framework governing relations between the two parties, including provisions on special rights, privileges and immunities for ecclesiastical officeholders and Catholic faithful in Ghana. Mr Ablakwa said the agreement aligns with the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations and addresses an outstanding issue between the Ghanaian government and the Apostolic Nunciature. He praised officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for their efforts in advancing the agreement and acknowledged the support of President John Dramani Mahama and the Attorney-General in bringing the process to this stage. Following Cabinet’s approval, Parliament is expected to consider the agreement for ratification under Article 75 of the 1992 Constitution. Ghana’s formal diplomatic relationship with the Holy See predates the arrival of the country’s first Apostolic Nuncio in 1976. Mr Ablakwa also recognised the Catholic Church’s contribution to national development, highlighting its work in education and healthcare through institutions serving communities across Ghana.

items.title: Admiral McRaven: Public Execution Is Shameless and Ignoble
items.description: A 62-grain, 5.56-mm round leaves the barrel of a standard-issue M4 rifle at approximately 2,900 feet per second. When it strikes a human being, the results are violent, traumatic, and unpredictable. If Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has his way, such images will soon be broadcast to the American people. The Pentagon has announced that the execution of Nidal Hasan, the Army officer convicted of killing 13 fellow service members in a 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood, in Texas, will be livestreamed. According to Amnesty International, 17 people were publicly executed in 2025. Eleven of these were in Iran and six in Afghanistan. Is this what we have become? Iran? Afghanistan? Are we so weak, so insecure, that we must convince the world that we are still powerful by making a public spectacle of an execution? Or maybe Secretary Hegseth and President Trump intend this as a spectacle for the American people: a show of just how much testosterone the two men have surging through their veins. No one should shed a tear for Hasan. I certainly won’t. But if Hegseth thinks that this public display will somehow deter others from horrible acts of violence, he is mistaken. Terrorists seek attention above all. Publicizing Hasan’s death therefore could incite other extremists to do equally egregious acts. And it adds to the narrative, advanced by our enemies and ever more worrying to our allies, that the United States has lost its way. When Osama bin Laden was killed, President Obama made a point of not releasing photographs of his body. “It’s not who we are,” he said. All of us who were involved in the operation agreed. Not sharing the pictures was a recognition that we are better than the inhuman beings who do unconscionable things, that there was a difference between a legitimate exercise of government authority and a public display of coercive power. Now, with this announcement, we are lowering ourselves to the ranks of brutal and failing regimes. I teach a graduate class on national-security decision making. I give my students a framework for thinking about how to make difficult decisions. The first question they have to answer before they can get to the right decision is: Who are we as a nation ? It is an acknowledgement that all correct decisions, those that will benefit us in the long run, will flow from an understanding of our American values. Our values as a nation matter. It’s not naive to think that we should have a sense of propriety when carrying out the harsh business of justice; to believe in our national sense of honor; and to expect our leaders to behave with dignity, integrity, civility, and humility. These values build stronger, smarter, more humane societies. They engender good alliances. They drive trust in businesses and higher education and they inspire our men and women in uniform. In almost 40 years of service, I came to realize that Americans share a common longing to be seen as the good guys. We were proud that our parents or grandparents fought against Nazism and fascism. As a nation, we stood tall against totalitarianism and communism. A younger generation sacrificed to keep America safe after 9/11. We made mistakes along the way; we always do. But despite these stumbles, inevitable in a complicated and violent world, I never once doubted that within our DNA was a sense of nobility that shaped the American character. There is nothing noble about a public display of a government-sanctioned execution. With this decision, the Trump administration continues to undermine our national values. Our current leaders are shameless and ignoble. They have no sense of dignity or honor. They seem to believe that the performance of cruel power is what makes a nation great: the spectacle, the show, the crude theatrics of a tough guy. Nothing could be further from the truth. Just ask the oppressed people of Iran and Afghanistan.

items.title: Sahara : Washington étudie l’avenir de la MINURSO
items.description: À quelques semaines du vote du Conseil de sécurité sur le renouvellement du mandat de la MINURSO, les États-Unis examinent plusieurs scénarios concernant l’avenir de la mission onusienne au Sahara. Une réunion à huis clos a notamment réuni des chercheurs et universitaires à Washington pour alimenter les réflexions américaines. Le département d’État américain a organisé, le 9 octobre, une réunion à huis clos avec une dizaine de chercheurs et d’universitaires consacrée à l’avenir de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara (MINURSO), rapporte Africa Intelligence. Le mandat de la mission arrive à échéance le 31 octobre, date à laquelle le Conseil de sécurité doit se prononcer sur son renouvellement. Selon le média spécialisé, les consultations américaines portent sur plusieurs options. Washington envisagerait notamment une prolongation d’un an, un renouvellement pour une période plus courte, une révision des responsabilités de la mission, voire sa fin. La réunion avait pour objectif de fournir aux responsables américains chargés du dossier du Sahara différentes analyses avant les négociations autour du projet de résolution qui sera soumis au Conseil de sécurité. Parmi les participants figuraient notamment des représentants de l’International Crisis Group, du Washington Institute for Near East Policy ainsi que de l’université américaine Colgate University. Les invitations auraient été envoyées le 8 octobre au soir. Boulos et Waltz impliqués dans les consultations Les discussions interviennent alors que plusieurs responsables américains suivent directement le dossier. Selon Africa Intelligence, Massad Boulos, conseiller principal du président américain Donald Trump pour l’Afrique, ainsi que Michael Waltz, ambassadeur des États-Unis auprès des Nations unies, font partie des responsables impliqués dans ces consultations. L’objectif est notamment d’évaluer les différentes options avant les discussions au Conseil de sécurité. Le mandat de la MINURSO au cœur des discussions Créée en 1991, la MINURSO avait notamment pour mission d’organiser un référendum d’autodétermination au Sahara. Ce scrutin n’a finalement jamais été organisé, tandis que les efforts visant à parvenir à un règlement politique entre le Maroc et le Front Polisario se poursuivent. Les discussions d’octobre interviennent après la présentation du dernier rapport du secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, sur le Sahara, ainsi qu’un briefing de son envoyé personnel, Staffan de Mistura. Le Conseil de sécurité attend également une revue stratégique de l’avenir du mandat de la MINURSO, demandée dans le cadre de la résolution 2797, adoptée en octobre 2025. Le Maroc défend son initiative d’autonomie Dans ce contexte, le Maroc continue de défendre son initiative d’autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine comme base d’un règlement du différend et plaide également pour une évolution du rôle de la MINURSO. De son côté, le Front Polisario maintient sa revendication en faveur de l’autodétermination, incluant l’option d’un référendum. Le Conseil de sécurité doit se prononcer sur l’avenir de la mission le 31 octobre. La durée du prochain mandat, mais aussi l’étendue de ses responsabilités, figurent ainsi parmi les principaux enjeux des discussions à venir. The post Sahara : Washington étudie l’avenir de la MINURSO appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Luv FM Corporate Games 2026: Kumasi Central Prisons, Amanfiman Bank win big amid fun
items.description: Corporate institutions in the Ashanti Region gathered for yet another thrilling and energetic day at the Luv FM Corporate Games 2026. The event brought together more than 22 corporate institutions for sporting activities aimed at promoting physical fitness, workplace relationships and business networking. Activities on the day included football, volleyball, basketball, table tennis, Ludo, sack bag races, line-and-spoon races and penalty kicks for chief executives of participating companies. The event saw the Kumasi Central Prisons team emerging overall winners of the much-anticipated 2026 football competition. The team attributed their victory to discipline, determination and tactical changes during the match. Speaking after the victory, leader of the group, Deputy Superintendent of Prisons, Richmond Oppong, said the players remained focused despite having only three days of training ahead of the competition. He indicated that the team’s defensive discipline and strategic substitutions to overpower their opponents saw them perform peerlessly and tactically on the field despite locking horns with Rango Construction Limited. “The main strategy for us was dedication and the referee was our challenge, but we still managed to secure the win,” he said. DSP Oppong further expressed excitement about the achievement and confidence in defending the trophy in future editions. Other winners of the day’s activities included Amenfiman Community Bank, which won the table tennis and volleyball competitions, while GLICO emerged winners of the line-and-spoon race and draft competition. CKM won the chief executives’ penalty kicks contest. Marketing and Relationship Manager at the Kumasi Unit of the Multimedia Group Limited, Maxwell Frimpong Manso, said the initiative was designed to encourage workers to stay physically active. He also highlighted that the event created opportunities for businesses to build relationships and explore partnerships outside their usual work environment. He further commended the sponsors and partners for supporting the event through funding, products, refreshments and other services, while encouraging more businesses to participate in future editions. “We appreciate several businesses also supporting the event through sponsorship, refreshments, products and other services,” he noted. Participating businesses also described the games as a valuable platform for promoting their products and services, increasing brand visibility and engaging potential customers. They said the event created opportunities to introduce new products, generate customer interest and establish business connections. The businesses were optimistic that the games would provide more opportunities for corporate engagement, product promotion and business-to-business partnerships. The Luv FM Corporate Games form part of the station’s efforts to bring corporate institutions together through sports, recreation and networking while providing businesses with opportunities to connect with wider audiences. The event received support from several corporate partners and sponsors, including Meera Company Limited, BonAgro Limited, Conkfans Company Limited, General Dentessa Limited, Mid City Dental Clinic, and Coca-Cola. Others are Ecobank, Royal Basin Hotel, Amenfiman Community Bank, Oak Specialist Hospital, Medimoses Day-to-Day Eye Clinic, Optimal Medical Diagnosis, Rango Construction Limited, and Astolinks.

items.title: Amgen, géant américain de la biotechnologie, s’allie à l’Algérie contre les maladies cardiovasculaires
items.description: Amgen, le géant américain de la biotechnologie, renforce ses positions en Algérie. La société de biotechnologie californienne a signé en fin de la semaine passée un mémorandum d’entente avec le ministère de la Santé en Algérie, pour renforcer la prévention des maladies cardiovasculaires qui représentent la première cause de mortalité en Algérie. « Cette étape importante reflète notre engagement commun en faveur de la promotion de la santé et de la prévention des maladies cardiovasculaires », a déclaré Yasmine Ait Yahia, directrice générale d’Amgen Algérie. Amgen est l’un des plus grands groupes biopharmaceutiques au monde. La société basée en Californie prévoit de réaliser un chiffre d’affaires de près de 40 milliards de dollars en 2026. Maladies cardiovasculaires, principal tueur en Algérie « Depuis de nombreuses années, Amgen est engagée au service des patients en Algérie. Cet accord témoigne de l'importance que nous accordons à la prévention, à la sensibilisation aux facteurs de risque cardiovasculaires et au développement d'initiatives contribuant à améliorer durablement la santé des patients », a ajouté la patronne de la filiale algérienne du géant américain de biotechnologie. Pour faire face aux maladies cardiovasculaires qui représentent 34% des causes de décès en Algérie, le ministre de la Santé, Mohamed Seddik Ait Messaoudène a installé en juin dernier une commission nationale spécialisée dont la mission est de moderniser l’organisation des soins, moderniser les plateaux techniques et réduire les inégalités d’accès aux traitements à travers le pays. Le s maladies cardiovasculaires constituent désormais le « principal défi pour la santé publique, et figurent parmi les principales causes de décès », avait indiqué le ministère de la Santé. items.title: Présidentielle en France : Raphaël Glucksmann remporte la primaire de la gauche non mélenchoniste
items.description: a l'issue d'un vote sans suspens, mais dont le resultat fait la une de la presse francaise ce 11 octobre, Raphael Glucksmann a remporte la primaire dite « sociale-democrate » avec 66,13% des suffrages, loin devant Olivier Faure et ses 14,46%. Sur la derniere marche du podium figure Segolene Royal, qui a obtenu 7,62% des suffrages, suivie de Emmanuel Maurel avec 5,92% des votes puis de Jerome Guedj avec 5,83%. Le copresident de Place publique etait donne gagnant , credite de 33 % des intentions de vote, par un sondage Harris Interactive publie le 9 octobre, jour d'ouverture de cette primaire qui a ete prolonge jusqu'a ce 11 octobre apres l'annonce d'une cyberattaque contre la plateforme de vote. En tout, 140 000 personnes s'etaient inscrites pour voter a cette primaire, bien loin des 2,8 millions de votants lors de la primaire de 2012 qui avait mis en lice Francois Hollande. Francois Hollande en embuscade ? Reste a savoir comment performera Raphael Glucksmann face a l'autre candidat de la gauche : le leader de La France insoumise Jean-Luc Melenchon. Jusqu'a present donne perdant – dans la plupart des sondages – face au dernier tribun de la vie politique francaise, Raphael Glucksmann affirmait debut juin qu'il « plie[rait] » Melenchon dans un match a gauche au premier tour. Une affirmation d'autant plus piquante que le charisme du candidat social-democrate est objet de railleries en France. Railleries qui viennent tant de ses opposants politiques, a l'instar du president des Republicains Bruno Retailleau, selon lequel Raphael Glucksmann aurait « le charisme d'un horodateur en panne », que de son propre camp : « Le gars qui pretend tenir tete a Poutine, il a ses antiseches sur son portable », taclait ainsi Segolene Royal. Raphael Glucksmann pourrait neanmoins avoir a composer avec une « inconnue », selon une partie de la presse francaise : Francois Hollande et ses velleites de retour a l'elysee. Celui-ci « parie sur un effondrement de Raphael Glucksmann d'ici au mois de janvier pour apparaître comme une solution de recours », peut-on ainsi lire. Reste a savoir si celui-ci voudra vraiment etre celui qui ecopera de l'ardoise budgetaire et sociale des deux quinquennats Macron.

items.title: Fazl accuses govt of reneging on its commitments after seeking his mediation with PTI
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman — who was being cast as the man who could defuse tensions between the Centre and the PTI until Sunday — has accused the government of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts for mediating between the two parties. Both sides held separate meetings with Fazl ahead of their political tensions culminating into the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where the PTI was in power. Addressing a press conference on Sunday, Fazl shared details of his engagement with both sides at a press conference held at his residence in Islamabad following an emergency meeting of the party’s Central Core Committee. He said he returned from Umrah on Oct 7, after which opposition leaders approached him and asked him to play a role in resolving the political impasse. The following day, he continued, federal ministers also visited him and sought his intervention. Tensions between the two sides had risen since the PTI announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. An impasse had emerged after talks between the two sides failed to yield any positive outcomes last week, following which the PTI began its march but remained within KP. Meanwhile, several federal ministers spoke about the possibility of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, linking it with the province’s security situation and the PTI’s alleged non-cooperation on counterterrorism. At the press conference on Sunday, Fazl said the PTI’s march had avoided entering Islamabad at his request and the government’s plan to impose emergency was deferred after its delegation approached him. “Subsequently, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif invited me to the Prime Minister House for a meeting. Although I felt the government had already made up its mind, my colleagues advised me to meet the prime minister,” he said. He said the government had insisted that the long march be called off first while the PTI demanded that its leaders be allowed to meet Imran in jail and court order regarding his transfer to a private hospital be implemented. Both sides were insisting that the other should take the first step, Fazl recalled. “I asked both sides to authorise me to act as a mediator and make decisions to move the process forward,” he said, adding that he also wanted to take now dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi into confidence. He said he held a conference call with Afridi, PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI leader Asad Qaiser, among others. Fazl said that during the conversation, he asked the KP chief minister whether the PTI was willing to end its long march if its demands were accepted. “Sohail Afridi said that if the demands were accepted, they would call off the long march.” Fazl said he had also visited the Prime Minister House and informed him that the PTI was ready to end its march if its demands were met. “I asked the prime minister to give an assurance that the PTI would be allowed to meet Imran Khan, and Imran Khan will receive the required medical treatment,” he said. The JUI-F chief said also intended to travel to Peshawar to hold further discussions with Afridi and other stakeholders, and that he wanted to involve two representatives each from the PTI and the PML-N in the negotiations under his “supervision to advance the process”. However, he said, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called him during the cabinet meeting on Sunday and informed him that the government wanted to impose an emergency in KP because of the security situation. “I questioned the rationale behind the proposed measure, pointing out that the security situation in Balochistan was worse than in KP, yet the government had not imposed governor’s rule there.” Fazl then accused the government of reneging on its commitments despite agreeing to a proposed course of action, saying he had questioned Dar about the purpose of seeking his mediation if the cabinet intended to make its own decision. “I asked Dar why I was asked to mediate if the cabinet was going to make the decision on its own,” he said. Asked whether politicians were responsible for the failure of negotiations, the JUI-F chief said the question should be put to the prime minister. “Ask Shehbaz Sharif how much authority he had during the negotiations,” he said. He further alleged that the government had created obstacles in the way of negotiations. ‘Attack on democracy’ Fazl also rejected the government’s move to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, terming it an “attack on democracy and the rights of the people”. “We reject the entire decision, word for word,” he said. The JUI-F chief said his party would challenge the decision through all available democratic and constitutional forums, including Parliament and the courts. “We will defend the Constitution, human rights and democratic rights in this country through constitutional and democratic platforms available to us,” he said. “We are not prepared to bow, even for a moment, before such unconstitutional measures.” He also regretted the PPP’s role in matter, describing it as one that undermined the Constitution and democracy. Reiterating that “we stand firmly with the Constitution of Pakistan”, he went on to refer to military operations over the year, beginning from the tenure of former military ruler retired General Pervez Musharraf to the present day. This strategy had repeatedly failed, he said. Responding to a question about the provincial government’s performance in KP, Fazl said that if the KP government had failed, the situation in Balochistan was worse. Asked if the opposition would resign from the assemblies, Fazl said the decision would be considered when the situation arose.

items.title: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack
items.description: A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, a day after another attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations at the facility. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war , where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis. The group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group “carried out four qualitative operations in the past 24 hours using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones”. Saree said they targeted the Riyadh airport multiple times, as well as the Dammam airport and two facilities belonging to the Saudi state oil company Aramco. Hours later, the Saudi coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire. Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added. The civil aviation authority said the attack caused an unspecified number of injuries, and that a damage assessment was underway. AFP journalists and locals reported hearing the sound of multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday. “The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city. ‘Full-fledged war crime’ The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport — where three people were also killed on Thursday — as well as on other key targets in the world’s top crude oil exporter. And although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through. “Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves against Houthi attacks,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University. The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”. Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday. Saturday’s attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the “horrific terrorist attack”. Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 wounded. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before. A Riyadh-based Western diplomat told AFP the official number of injured may not give a full picture, as it did not appear to include those with minor wounds. Operations suspended Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source said, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 21:00 GMT (2am PKT on Monday). A second aviation source confirmed the halt in operations “until further notice”, adding radar and communications equipment was damaged and runways needed to be assessed. Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath. “People who were in Terminal 3 started running towards us,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP . “Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood.” The attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said. The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport, while Australia urged its citizens on Sunday to stay indoors altogether and “shelter in place”. The Houthis also claimed to have targeted the Dammam airport, whose official website on Sunday showed many flights — both departures and arrivals — were delayed. ‘Rewrite the rules’ Saturday’s airport strike, on the eve of Saudi Arabia’s high-profile convention and entertainment season, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing. With the summer heat subsiding, October also usually marks the beginning of the high season for Umrah pilgrims, with millions of Muslims from across the world flocking to Makkah. Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa. Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to rewrite the rules of the game”. “They want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them,” he said. “So if their airport in Sanaa has to be closed because of the Saudi air embargo, they want to do the same thing to Saudi Arabia.” On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said on Saturday. The Houthis claimed to have repelled them. Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

Centrafrique : la Télévision centrafricaine se dote d’un nouveau studio pour mieux «porter la voix de la République»
items.description: La Television centrafricaine s'est dotee d'un nouveau studio moderne, baptise « la 7ᵉ Republique », dont l'inauguration a ete effectuee le 9 octobre lors d'une ceremonie presidee par le Premier ministre, Felix Moloua, avec la presence de plusieurs membres du gouvernement, dont le ministre de l'Urbanisme, Hassane Bouba Ali, et le ministre d'etat a la Communication, le Dr Evariste Ngamana, maître d'œuvre du projet, selon la presse locale. « Aujourd'hui, nous ne receptionnons pas seulement un studio. Nous posons un acte de souverainete. La communication gouvernementale est le pilier de la transparence et de la bonne gouvernance. On ne peut pas parler de 7ᵉ Republique avec des outils de la 1ʳᵉ Republique », a declare le Dr Evariste Ngamana. Les medias publics comme instrument « d'information, d'education, de culture et de cohesion nationale » Le ministre de la Communication centrafricain a fait part de la volonte du gouvernement de faire de ses medias publics de « veritables instruments d'information, d'education, de culture et de cohesion nationale ». Dans ce contexte, il a explique : « Nous ne pouvons pas demander a nos medias publics de porter la voix de la Republique, d'accompagner les transformations de notre pays et de repondre aux exigences du numerique avec des outils qui appartiennent parfois a une autre epoque. » « Notre ambition est de faire mieux, de produire davantage de contenus de qualite, d'etre plus proches des citoyens », a-t-il souligne. Projet concretise grâce au partenariat public-prive D'apres le Dr Evariste Ngamana, la vetuste des equipements dont dispose la tele nationale avait rendu necessaire la recherche de nouvelles solutions. C'est dans ce cadre que le projet a ete mis sur pied grâce a un partenariat public-prive, mettant a profit l'expertise de l'entreprise Descom, qui a finance la rehabilitation du studio. Des investissements ont egalement ete consacres a l'autonomie energetique des stations dans le but de limiter les interruptions d'antenne causees par les coupures d'electricite, selon le ministre. Des l'inauguration du studio, cette nouvelle structure a accueilli un grand debat diffuse en direct par la Television centrafricaine, durant lequel les ministres presents se sont succedes sur le plateau pour defendre leur bilan et repondre aux questions des journalistes et des telespectateurs.

items.title: A Spot-On SNL Parody About Men Who Can’t Deal With Time’s Passage
items.description: Even if you don’t know much country music, you likely know how much the genre loves the trope of the weepy father at his daughter’s wedding. In the best sketch of last night’s Saturday Night Live , the father of the bride was played by the host, Shane Gillis, but he wasn’t reflecting on life’s heavy milestones. Instead, he was thinking about “all the cool shit I can put in her room.” As narrated by a Rascal Flatts–esque band (composed of Andrew Dismukes, James Austin Johnson, and Tommy Brennan), the dad imagined everything he was going to put in his new man cave: a Ms. Pac-Man machine and a pinball machine; a drum set that he swore he would finally learn to play; a life-size cutout of Shaquille O’Neal; a bottle of lotion and box of tissues (a bit stolen from the Paul Rudd film I Love You, Man); a House box set; a cotton-candy machine. A child’s wedding is a joyous occasion, a new chapter for the family. But any beginning also reminds us that time’s arrow stubbornly points in only one direction. The sketch smartly underscored how many American men use consumer goods to distract themselves from anxieties about aging and the creeping sense that life may pass them by. Why deal with your uneasy feelings when you can finally afford the replica of a Star Wars stormtrooper you’ve wanted—nay, deserved—since you were a teenager? The hit of dopamine from a shopping spree is certainly more fun than wrestling with where your life currently stands. The best SNL song sketches expand on a central idea as the parody progresses, commenting on the characters’ comedic dilemmas. They also need to nail the musical references (Tim McGraw, Alan Jackson, Zac Brown, and, yes, Rascal Flatts have all released songs on this theme, something that the southerners Dismukes and Johnson are likely aware of). In last night’s sketch, we learned that Gillis’s presumably long-suffering wife (Ashley Padilla) “hates my room / we’re drifting apart,” and that she’s becoming a bit too close with her Zumba instructor, Tad (Marcello Hernández), “who’s actually pretty cool”—an off-hand remark from a man too clueless to see what’s coming next. Whatever you think about him, last night’s host was well equipped for this exploration of male obliviousness. [ Read: What Shane Gillis proved on SNL ] In 2019, Gillis was set to join SNL before some of his old offensive jokes resurfaced and NBC rescinded the offer . Gillis apologized for the material, and SNL ’s creator, Lorne Michaels, indicated that the casting decision was out of his hands . Michaels seems to have some lingering regrets about how it all went down; last night was Gillis’s third time hosting. But this overcorrection is arguably not doing Gillis many favors, as the episode often demonstrated his limitations as a comedian . He flubbed most of his lines—and cursed—in a sketch parodying Green Eggs and Ham , then apologized “about earlier” during the episode’s closing goodbyes. Gillis tends to embody characters who aren’t actively hateful or toxic but just a little confused about society’s changing social mores and unsure about what they’re allowed to say. But Gillis, who lacks the dexterity of clear influences such as Louis C.K. and Dave Chappelle, can’t consistently pull off that tricky balance of thoughtfulness and provocation. During his opening monologue, in a bit about struggling to seem nonthreatening when he encounters a woman on an otherwise solitary hike, he lost the audience after saying, “I haven’t been to the gym in so long I didn’t know women just dress like whores now?” (I’ll spare you his description of women’s modern athleisure wear.) By that point, the crowd was so cold he couldn’t win it back with a clever closing riff about society’s polarization and the dangers of ambiguous haircuts: “You’re either gay or you’re Hitler, and isn’t that where we’re at as a country?” Still, Gillis has become a successful touring comedian, mostly because he is very good at expressing the immaturity, simmering hostility, and general dunderheadedness of a certain strain of American manhood. His best sketches from last night made use of that meathead persona, as when he played a jerky police officer hosting the discussion show Cop Talk and the manager of an HVAC company that prided itself on having the most off-putting employees you would ever encounter. But the wedding-song sketch stood out because it zeroed in on the stunted emotional life of Gillis’s character and then mocked it relentlessly. After his wife left him for Tad, he decided to build an even bigger room of one’s own (“Super Room Rocks!”), but when the impromptu construction project exposed him to black mold, he began “tripping balls.” The story eventually took an unexpectedly frisky turn before the episode’s kicker revealed this entire misadventure was a dream sequence that began after he forgot to help his daughter and wife pack up the moving van—a sly commentary on the character’s misplaced priorities. It’s hard to say whether Gillis found success because he’s secretly very perceptive about the state of modern masculinity or because he’s unafraid to admit just how unperceptive he is about the modern world. Either way, last night’s song fulfilled the country-music imperative of “three chords and the truth”: a catchy ballad about how many men are emotionally stunted and unable to deal with aging and change, and will instead retreat into materialism and adolescent interests rather than reconcile with life’s relentless momentum.
